1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# accounts.sh — the owner's command for the live accounts file.
     3	#
     4	# Usage:
     5	#   accounts.sh list [--json]
     6	#   accounts.sh get <name> [field]
     7	#   accounts.sh set <name> <field> <value>     ceiling|reserved|enabled|note|label|
     8	#                                              endpoint|codex_home
     9	#   accounts.sh enable <name>  [--note TEXT]
    10	#   accounts.sh disable <name> [--note TEXT]
    11	#   accounts.sh add <name> --endpoint E --codex-home D --ceiling N
    12	#                          [--label L] [--reserved N] [--note TEXT] [--disabled]
    13	#   accounts.sh remove <name>
    14	#   accounts.sh cap <name> <n>                 set the EFFECTIVE cap now
    15	#   accounts.sh probe [name] [--force] [--dry-run]
    16	#   accounts.sh seed                           write the file from the brief (once)
    17	#   accounts.sh apply-directives --text-file F apply ACCOUNTS: lines from a file
    18	#   accounts.sh log [-n N]
    19	#
    20	# What it edits: ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json, the live source of
    21	# truth for which keys exist, what their CEILINGS are, and whether the pipeline may
    22	# use them.  The capacity controller and account_router.py re-read that file every
    23	# tick and every reservation, so a change here reaches admission within 60 seconds
    24	# with no session prompted, no brief re-applied and nothing restarted.
    25	#
    26	# `ceiling` is a ceiling and never a target: the controller's AIMD discovery runs
    27	# below it and may never exceed `ceiling - external_reserved`.  Lowering it takes
    28	# effect at the next tick; raising it lets the additive creep continue.
    29	# `enabled false` is cap 0 immediately and no probes, and so is `remove`.
    30	#
    31	# Raising a ceiling is a PERMISSION, not a jump: AIMD then creeps +1 per quiet
    32	# window (120 s by default) and only while the key is saturated, so ten recovered
    33	# slots take twenty minutes of real demand.  `accounts.sh cap <name> <n>` is the
    34	# one immediate lever — it sets the effective cap now, clamped to the ceiling and
    35	# recorded by the controller.  Set the ceiling first; the cap cannot exceed it.
    36	#
    37	# Every write is atomic (temp file + rename) and appends one line to
    38	# ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/capacity/accounts.log.  No key value is ever
    39	# stored in the file: an entry names the codex home the key lives in, nothing more.
    40	#
    41	# `probe` runs one bounded read-only health probe per account through the capacity
    42	# controller (the owner of endpoint health) and prints what it found; it is how a
    43	# key disabled by measured health is checked by hand instead of waited on.  It
    44	# spends one real session per key, so it REFUSES while the run is paused or the
    45	# caps are held; `--force` says it anyway and `--dry-run` runs nothing at all.
    46	#
    47	# This is a thin, versioned wrapper: every rule above is enforced by
    48	# local/bin/accounts_file.py, so the CLI and the janitor's GitHub channel cannot
    49	# disagree about what a valid entry is.
    50	#
    51	# Environment: MIPSTARRE_CHECKOUT (checkout holding local/bin; default the recorded
    52	# owner-bin/repo-root, then ~/MIPStarRE-qpbt), MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT.
    53	#
    54	# Exit codes: 0 ok · 2 usage, an invalid file or an invalid value (nothing written)
    55	#             · 3 no such account · 4 no checkout found
    56	set -u
    57	
    58	PROG="accounts.sh"
    59	CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
    60	OWNER_BIN="${MIPSTARRE_OWNER_BIN:-$CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin}"
    61	
    62	usage() { sed -n '2,55p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    63	
    64	resolve_root() {
    65	  local candidate
    66	  for candidate in "${MIPSTARRE_CHECKOUT:-}" "${MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT:-}"; do
    67	    [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -f "$candidate/local/bin/accounts_file.py" ] && {
    68	      printf '%s\n' "$candidate"; return 0; }
    69	  done
    70	  if [ -r "$OWNER_BIN/repo-root" ]; then
    71	    candidate="$(cat "$OWNER_BIN/repo-root")"
    72	    [ -f "$candidate/local/bin/accounts_file.py" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$candidate"; return 0; }
    73	  fi
    74	  # Running from the checkout itself (results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh).
    75	  candidate="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"
    76	  [ -n "$candidate" ] && [ -f "$candidate/local/bin/accounts_file.py" ] && {
    77	    printf '%s\n' "$candidate"; return 0; }
    78	  candidate="$HOME/MIPStarRE-qpbt"
    79	  [ -f "$candidate/local/bin/accounts_file.py" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$candidate"; return 0; }
    80	  return 1
    81	}
    82	
    83	case "${1:-}" in
    84	  -h|--help|"") usage; [ -n "${1:-}" ] && exit 0 || exit 2 ;;
    85	esac
    86	
    87	ROOT="$(resolve_root)" || {
    88	  printf '%s: no checkout with local/bin/accounts_file.py found. Set MIPSTARRE_CHECKOUT.\n' \
    89	    "$PROG" >&2
    90	  exit 4
    91	}
    92	
    93	# The version banner every installed tool prints (owner-tools/README.md).  It goes
    94	# to stderr so `accounts.sh get second ceiling` stays usable in a shell expression.
    95	VERSION="$( { [ -s "$OWNER_BIN/tools-version" ] &&
    96	    sed -n 's/.*short=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "$OWNER_BIN/tools-version" | head -n 1; } ||
    97	  git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    98	printf 'tool=%s version=%s\n' "$PROG" "${VERSION:-unknown}" >&2
    99	
   100	ACTOR="${MIPSTARRE_ACCOUNTS_ACTOR:-${USER:-owner}}"
   101	
   102	command="$1"; shift
   103	case "$command" in
   104	  probe)
   105	    # "$@" carries the optional account plus --force/--dry-run; a name is
   106	    # [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31} (accounts_file.NAME_RE), so it never begins with
   107	    # '-' and anything that does is reported by the controller's own parser.
   108	    exec python3 "$ROOT/local/bin/capacity_controller.py" probe "$@"
   109	    ;;
   110	  cap)
   111	    [ "$#" -eq 2 ] || {
   112	      printf '%s: usage: accounts.sh cap <name> <n>  (the ceiling is set with "set")\n' \
   113	        "$PROG" >&2; exit 2; }
   114	    case "$1" in
   115	      ''|[!a-z0-9]*|*[!a-z0-9_-]*)
   116	        printf '%s: %s is not an account name ([a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31})\n' "$PROG" "$1" >&2
   117	        exit 2 ;;
   118	    esac
   119	    exec python3 "$ROOT/local/bin/capacity_controller.py" set "$1" "$2"
   120	    ;;
   121	  log)
   122	    LINES=50
   123	    case "${1:-}" in -n) LINES="${2:-50}" ;; esac
   124	    LOG="$CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/capacity/accounts.log"
   125	    [ -s "$LOG" ] || { printf '%s: no edits recorded yet (%s)\n' "$PROG" "$LOG"; exit 0; }
   126	    exec tail -n "$LINES" "$LOG"
   127	    ;;
   128	  list|get|set|enable|disable|add|remove|seed|apply-directives)
   129	    exec python3 "$ROOT/local/bin/accounts_file.py" --actor "$ACTOR" "$command" "$@"
   130	    ;;
   131	  *)
   132	    printf '%s: unknown command %s\n\n' "$PROG" "$command" >&2
   133	    usage >&2
   134	    exit 2
   135	    ;;
   136	esac

    74	### The owner's personal cron scripts
    75	
    76	These stay in `~/bin` on the host — they are the owner's, not the pipeline's — and
    77	`install-crons.sh` writes their crontab rows only when the run mode asks for them
    78	(`cron.watchdog`, `cron.heartbeat`, `cron.astra_poll`; all `off` since 2026-09-09).

    80	| Host path | Source of truth | Status |
    81	|---|---|---|

    86	
    87	## The owner's five commands
    88	
    89	```sh
    90	owner-bin/owner-pause.sh  [--deadline 15m] [--reason "..."] [--dry-run]
    91	owner-bin/owner-resume.sh [--dry-run] [--force-crontab]
    92	owner-bin/owner-say.sh --mode idle|interrupt|terminal [--timeout N] "TEXT"
    93	owner-bin/install-crons.sh [--paused] [--dry-run] [--restore FILE]
    94	owner-bin/accounts.sh     list | get | set | enable | disable | add | remove | probe | log
    95	```
    96	
    97	### `accounts.sh` — the keys, their ceilings and their health
    98	
    99	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json` is the **live** source of truth for
   100	admission: one entry per key, `{name, label, endpoint, codex_home, ceiling,
   101	external_reserved, enabled, note}`, any number of endpoints and keys. The capacity
   102	controller and `account_router.py` re-read it every tick and every reservation, so an edit
   103	reaches admission within 60 seconds with **no session prompted, no brief re-applied and
   104	nothing restarted**. `run_mode.py apply` seeds the file from the brief when it is absent and
   105	never overwrites an existing one.
   106	
   107	```sh
   108	accounts.sh list                                  # every key, its ceiling and its state
   109	accounts.sh set second ceiling 20                 # the admin took slots back
   110	accounts.sh set second reserved 4                 # a forked session shares this key
   111	accounts.sh disable second --note "quota gone"    # cap 0 immediately, no probes
   112	accounts.sh enable second
   113	accounts.sh add third --endpoint api.third.example \
   114	    --codex-home ~/.codex-third --ceiling 8       # routable at the next reservation
   115	accounts.sh remove third
   116	accounts.sh probe second                          # one read-only health probe, now
   117	accounts.sh log -n 20                             # who changed what, and when
   118	```
   119	
   120	* **`ceiling` is a ceiling, never a target.** The controller's AIMD discovery runs below it
   121	  and may never exceed `ceiling - external_reserved`. Lowering it takes effect at the next
   122	  tick; raising it lets the additive creep continue — the cap does not leap to the new
   123	  number. A run sitting at 60 % of the ceiling with no refusals is behaving correctly.
   124	* **`external_reserved == ceiling` is legal** and means the key has no slot for the pipeline
   125	  right now — an honest state during a run, and different from `enabled: false`, which is a
   126	  decision.
   127	* **No key value is ever stored.** An entry names the codex home the key lives in; the
   128	  secret stays in that directory, which only the owner touches.
   129	* Every write is atomic (temp file + rename) and appends one line to
   130	  `watchdog/capacity/accounts.log`. A bad field is refused with the field named and the file
   131	  is left byte-identical, so the controller reading it a millisecond later never sees a
   132	  half-file.
   133	
   134	**From GitHub, when there is no shell.** A comment on the owner inbox issue in the fixed
   135	form `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]` (one or more lines
   136	per comment) is applied by `local/bin/janitor.sh` at its next sweep and answered with one
   137	reply saying exactly what took effect (`applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20`, or `rejected: …`
   138	with the reason). Only comments written by the repository owner login recorded in
   139	`local/README.md` are applied; anyone else's are answered with a `rejected:` line naming
   140	them. The channel carries `ceiling`, `reserved`, `enabled` and `note` only — an endpoint or
   141	a codex home is a path on the host and is set here, where a typo cannot travel through a
   142	public comment.
   143	
   144	**Measured health.** A key that answers `401`/`403`/invalid-key or `INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`
   145	disables itself at the first occurrence, and an endpoint answering 5xx three times in two
   146	minutes does the same; both record the REASON in `watchdog/capacity/health.json` and cap the
   147	key at 0. A disabled key probes its own way back (read-only, bounded, single-flight) and
   148	returns at cap 1, never at its pre-outage cap. The hourly readiness report on the progress
   149	issue carries one line per key — ceiling, effective cap, live, refusals in the last ten
   150	minutes, health with its reason, and the owner's own note — so none of this needs a question
   151	to a session.
   152	
   153	### `owner-pause.sh` — pause within the deadline
   154	
   155	The deadline comes from `run.pause_deadline_min` in the run brief; no timestamp is written
   156	into the script. `--dry-run` prints the phase plan and the computed deadline and touches
   157	nothing.
   158	
   159	| T | Phase |
   160	|---|---|
   161	| +0:00 | `run_mode.py pause` — caps to 0, pre-pause caps saved **inside** `capacity/state.json`; `touch watchdog/drain` |

   109	class DrainRequested(Exception):
   110	    """``watchdog/drain`` appeared while this dispatch was queued.
   111	
   112	    The pause path touches that file, and a queued dispatch must then release
   113	    itself: on 2026-09-12 forty-nine waiters sat behind twelve workers and the
   114	    pause could only clear them by killing the processes, which threw away the
   115	    dispatch requests with them.

   119	def choose_account(live: list[int], caps: list[int],
   120	                   names: tuple[str, ...] = DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS) -> str:
   121	    """The account with the most headroom, as a fraction of its own cap.
   122	
   123	    The rule is unchanged for two accounts — ``live[0]*caps[1] <= live[1]*caps[0]``
   124	    is exactly "the first account's occupancy is no higher" — and generalizes to
   125	    N by comparing ``live/cap`` as a fraction, with ties going to the earlier
   126	    entry so a two-account file keeps preferring ``primary``.  A zero cap is
   127	    never chosen: `reserve` has already filtered it out, and treating it as
   128	    infinitely free is how a dead endpoint attracted every dispatch.
   129	    """
   130	    best, best_key = names[0], None
   131	    for index, name in enumerate(names):
   132	        cap = caps[index]
   133	        if cap <= 0:
   134	            continue
   135	        key = (live[index] * 1.0 / cap, index)
   136	        if best_key is None or key < best_key:
   137	            best, best_key = name, key
   138	    return best

   141	def health_state(root: Path, account: str) -> str:
   142	    """Endpoint health as ``capacity_controller.py`` last recorded it.
   143	
   144	    Absent, unreadable or unrecognized is ``up``: with no controller running the
   145	    router behaves exactly as it did before this field existed, and the cap
   146	    files alone govern admission.
   147	    """
   148	    path = root / "watchdog" / "capacity" / f"health-{account}.json"
   149	    try:
   150	        document = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   151	    except (OSError, ValueError):
   152	        return "up"
   153	    state = document.get("state") if isinstance(document, dict) else None
   154	    return state if state in ("up", "degraded", "down") else "up"

   157	def disabled_accounts(root: Path) -> set[str]:
   158	    """Names the owner's live file marks ``enabled: false``, or has dropped.
   159	
   160	    Belt and braces with the capacity controller, which writes cap 0 for such an
   161	    account at its next tick: between the owner's edit and that tick — up to 60
   162	    seconds — the cap file still holds the old number, and a dispatch admitted in
   163	    that window runs on a key the owner has just taken away.  Reading the file
   164	    here closes the window.  It can only ever narrow admission.
   165	    """
   166	    try:
   167	        import accounts_file  # noqa: PLC0415 - same directory, optional
   168	        entries = accounts_file.load(root)
   169	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - an unreadable file changes nothing
   170	        return set()
   171	    if entries is None:
   172	        return set()
   173	    return {entry["name"] for entry in entries if not entry["enabled"]}

   176	def effective_caps(root: Path, names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None) -> list[int]:
   177	    """Per-account caps, with a dead, disabled or homeless account forced to zero.
   178	
   179	    Without the health part the router *prefers* the dead account:
   180	    `choose_account` picks the lower live/cap ratio, and an endpoint answering
   181	    503 keeps freeing slots as its sessions die, so every new dispatch is routed
   182	    into the outage.  That is how one hour of relay-us7 503s cost 69 sessions on
   183	    2026-09-12.  Forcing the cap to zero only ever narrows admission; it can
   184	    never widen it.
   185	
   186	    **A name with no CODEX_HOME is cap 0.**  `account_names` deliberately falls
   187	    open to the ``max-codex-*`` glob when accounts.json is unreadable, so that a
   188	    mistyped ceiling cannot stop admission — but `account_homes` reads the same
   189	    file and has no such glob, so in exactly that window a third key was
   190	    admitted here while `dispatch.sh` could not resolve its home and ran the
   191	    worker on the ambient ``~/.codex``.  The owner's ceiling of 5 on the primary
   192	    key then carried cap(second) + cap(third) sessions, with the pipeline's own
   193	    accounting attributing them elsewhere.  Admitting only to a key whose home is
   194	    known closes that: the fail-open name list survives, and it can no longer
   195	    point at a key the dispatcher cannot actually reach.
   196	    """
   197	    accounts = names if names is not None else account_names(root)
   198	    disabled = disabled_accounts(root)
   199	    homes = account_homes(root)
   200	    caps = []
   201	    for account in accounts:
   202	        path = root / 'watchdog' / f'max-codex-{account}'
   203	        cap = int(path.read_text().strip()) if path.exists() else 0
   204	        if cap < 0:
   205	            raise ValueError(f'{path}: cap must be nonnegative')
   206	        if (account in disabled or account not in homes
   207	                or health_state(root, account) == "down"):
   208	            cap = 0
   209	        caps.append(cap)
   210	    return caps

   213	def live_pids(directory: Path) -> set[int]:
   214	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   215	    live = set()
   216	    for marker in directory.iterdir():
   217	        if not marker.name.isdecimal() or int(marker.name) <= 0 or not marker.is_file():
   218	            continue
   219	        try:
   220	            os.kill(int(marker.name), 0)
   221	        except ProcessLookupError:
   222	            marker.unlink(missing_ok=True)
   223	        except PermissionError:
   224	            live.add(int(marker.name))
   225	        else:
   226	            live.add(int(marker.name))
   227	    return live

   230	def session_rows(registry: Path) -> list[dict]:
   231	    """Share locked, malformed-row-tolerant history without discarding object metadata."""
   232	    rows = []
   233	    if registry.exists():
   234	        with registry.open(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
   235	            fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_SH)
   236	            for number, line in enumerate(handle, 1):
   237	                if not line.strip():
   238	                    continue
   239	                try:
   240	                    row = json.loads(line)
   241	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
   242	                    row = None
   243	                if not isinstance(row, dict):
   244	                    print(f"account routing: {registry}:{number}: "
   245	                          "skipping malformed registry record", file=sys.stderr)
   246	                    continue
   247	                rows.append(row)
   248	    return rows

   251	def is_account_name(value) -> bool:
   252	    """A syntactically valid account name.
   253	
   254	    Affinity and continuation are judged on the *recorded* name, not on today's
   255	    account list: a thread started on a key the owner has since retired still
   256	    belongs to that key, and the reservation for it will simply find no capacity.
   257	    Reading the historical row as "not an account" instead would silently turn a
   258	    resume into a fresh thread.
   259	    """
   260	    return isinstance(value, str) and bool(_NAME_RE.match(value))

   263	def resume_account(thread: str, registry: Path, homes: dict[str, Path]) -> str:
   264	    matches = {row['account'] for row in session_rows(registry)
   265	               if row.get('thread_id') == thread and is_account_name(row.get('account'))}
   266	    for account, home in homes.items():
   267	        for area in ("sessions", "archived_sessions"):
   268	            if any((home / area).rglob(f"rollout-*{thread}.jsonl")):
   269	                matches.add(account)
   270	    if len(matches) != 1:
   271	        raise ValueError(f"cannot establish unique resume account for {thread}")
   272	    return matches.pop()

   275	def resume_continuation(registry: Path, thread: str) -> dict:
   276	    """Carry the original snapshot and completed segments, deduplicating status appends."""
   277	    history = {}
   278	    for row in session_rows(registry):
   279	        if row.get('thread_id') != thread:
   280	            continue
   281	        if not row.get('name'):
   282	            # Legacy affinity rows have no session identity for charge deduplication.
   283	            if row.get('continuation', {}) != {}:
   284	                raise ValueError('invalid continuation metadata on unnamed registry record')
   285	            continue
   286	        history[row['name']] = row
   287	    prior = {}
   288	    for row in history.values():
   289	        metadata = row.get('continuation', {})
   290	        if not isinstance(metadata, dict) or (metadata and (
   291	                not metadata.get('budget_file') or not isinstance(metadata.get('budget'), dict) or
   292	                not {'anchor', 'attempt_limit', 'attempts', 'working_seconds', 'sessions'} <=
   293	                metadata['budget'].keys())):
   294	            raise ValueError('invalid continuation metadata')
   295	        if metadata:
   296	            prior = dict(metadata)
   297	        if prior:
   298	            prior['completed_wall_s'] = prior.get('completed_wall_s', 0) + row['wall_s']
   299	    return prior

   302	def resume_model(thread: str, registry: Path, homes: dict[str, Path]) -> str:
   303	    """Require observed model affinity; a new default cannot relabel an old thread."""
   304	    observed = [row.get('effective_model') for row in session_rows(registry)
   305	                if row.get('thread_id') == thread and row.get('effective_model')]
   306	    for home in homes.values():
   307	        for area in ('sessions', 'archived_sessions'):
   308	            for rollout in (home / area).rglob(f'rollout-*{thread}.jsonl'):
   309	                for row in session_rows(rollout):
   310	                    if row.get('type') == 'turn_context' and row.get('payload', {}).get('model'):
   311	                        observed.append(row['payload']['model'])
   312	    if not observed or len(set(observed)) != 1:
   313	        raise ValueError('resume model is unknown or mixed; use a fresh linked assignment')
   314	    return observed[0]

   317	def continuation(path: Path, registry: Path, worktree: Path, issue: str) -> dict:
   318	    """Validate an operator checkpoint handoff without changing the old thread or budget."""
   319	    request = json.loads(path.read_text())
   320	    rows = session_rows(registry)
   321	    previous = next(row for row in reversed(rows) if row.get('name') == request['previous_session'])
   322	    if (previous.get('status') not in ('done', 'failed', 'archived') or
   323	            not is_account_name(previous.get('account')) or not previous.get('thread_id') or
   324	            str(previous.get('issue')) != issue):
   325	        raise ValueError('continuation requires a terminal, same-issue predecessor with affinity')
   326	    checkpoint = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(worktree), 'rev-parse', '--verify',
   327	        '--end-of-options', request['checkpoint'] + '^{commit}'], text=True).strip()
   328	    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(worktree), 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor',
   329	                    checkpoint, 'HEAD'], check=True, capture_output=True)
   330	    budget_path = Path(request['budget_file']).resolve(strict=True)
   331	    budget = json.loads(budget_path.read_text())
   332	    if (not budget['anchor'] or previous['name'] not in budget['sessions'] or
   333	            not 0 < budget['attempts'] < budget['attempt_limit'] or
   334	            budget['working_seconds'] < previous.get('wall_s', 0)):
   335	        raise ValueError('continuation requires the shared, charged, unexhausted budget')
   336	    prior = resume_continuation(registry, previous['thread_id'])
   337	    if prior and (prior['budget_file'] != str(budget_path) or
   338	                  prior['budget']['anchor'] != budget['anchor'] or
   339	                  prior['budget']['attempt_limit'] != budget['attempt_limit'] or
   340	                  prior['budget']['attempts'] >= budget['attempts'] or
   341	                  prior['budget']['working_seconds'] + prior['completed_wall_s'] >
   342	                  budget['working_seconds']):
   343	        raise ValueError('continuation must retain its original budget and accumulated charges')
   344	    return dict(previous_session=previous['name'], previous_thread_id=previous['thread_id'],
   345	                previous_account=previous['account'], checkpoint=checkpoint,
   346	                budget_file=str(budget_path), budget=budget)

   349	def reserve(root: Path, requested: str, pid: int, wait: int, dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
   350	    """Reserve one worker slot under the lock shared by all dispatchers.
   351	
   352	    ``watchdog/drain`` is checked on every poll iteration, before the lock, and
   353	    raises `DrainRequested` so a queued dispatch releases itself during a pause
   354	    instead of being killed.  Absent file, absent health file: unchanged
   355	    behaviour in every respect.
   356	    """
   357	    if (requested != 'auto' and not is_account_name(requested)) or pid <= 0 or wait < 0:
   358	        raise ValueError('expected a valid account, positive pid and nonnegative wait')
   359	    accounts = root / "accounts"
   360	    accounts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   361	    deadline = time.monotonic() + wait
   362	    while True:
   363	        if (root / "watchdog" / "drain").exists():
   364	            raise DrainRequested('drain in progress; no reservation made')
   365	        with (accounts / "router.lock").open("a") as lock:
   366	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   367	            # Re-read per iteration, inside the lock: a waiter queued for half an
   368	            # hour must see the key the owner added, the ceiling they raised and
   369	            # the account they disabled, without being restarted.
   370	            names = account_names(root)
   371	            if requested != 'auto' and requested not in names:
   372	                raise ValueError(
   373	                    f'{requested!r} is not one of the configured accounts '
   374	                    f'({", ".join(names)}); add it with owner-tools/accounts.sh add')
   375	            caps = effective_caps(root, names)
   376	            live = [len(live_pids(accounts / account)) for account in names]
   377	            free = [index for index, account in enumerate(names)
   378	                    if live[index] < caps[index] and requested in ('auto', account)]
   379	            if free:
   380	                # Only the accounts with a free slot compete, exactly as the
   381	                # two-account form did: a full account is not a candidate.
   382	                selected = (names[free[0]] if len(free) == 1 else choose_account(
   383	                    [live[index] for index in free], [caps[index] for index in free],
   384	                    tuple(names[index] for index in free)))
   385	                if not dry_run:
   386	                    (accounts / selected / str(pid)).touch()
   387	                return selected
   388	            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
   389	            if dry_run or remaining <= 0:
   390	                raise ValueError('account capacity exhausted; no reservation made')
   391	        time.sleep(min(10, remaining))

   394	def main() -> None:
   395	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   396	    parser.add_argument("command", choices=("reserve",))
   397	    parser.add_argument("root", type=Path)
   398	    # Not `choices=`: the account set is on disk, not in this file, and a name
   399	    # the owner added minutes ago must be accepted.  `reserve` validates it
   400	    # against the live list and names the alternatives when it does not match.
   401	    parser.add_argument("account")

   417	            args.account = affinity

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""The owner's run briefing, validated once, and the mode file everything reads.
     3	
     4	One artifact states a run's capacity, schedule, speed and issue numbers: the
     5	brief the owner copies to ``~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/run-brief.json``
     6	from the committed template
     7	``results/telemetry/owner-tools/run-brief.template.json``.  ``apply`` validates
     8	it strictly and turns it into ``watchdog/run-mode.json``, the record every
     9	component reads through ``run_mode.py get KEY``.  No protocol, persona or
    10	script carries a literal cap, floor, cadence or issue number
    11	(``local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md``).
    12	
    13	Subcommands::
    14	
    15	    run_mode.py apply [--brief PATH] [--dry-run]
    16	    run_mode.py show [--json | --oneline]
    17	    run_mode.py get KEY
    18	    run_mode.py set speed fast|default [--dry-run]
    19	    run_mode.py pause [--reason TEXT]
    20	    run_mode.py resume
    21	
    22	``show --oneline`` renders the whole mode on one line; it is what the goal text
    23	(``owner-tools/goal-keeper.sh``) and the resume message
    24	(``owner-tools/owner-resume.sh``) carry, so neither has to name a number.
    25	
    26	``watchdog/account-mode`` is DERIVED from ``accounts[].enabled`` by ``apply``,
    27	``pause`` and ``resume`` — ``both`` when more than one account is enabled and
    28	``primary`` otherwise — because the deployed PATH shim reads it before it lets a
    29	dispatch use a second ``CODEX_HOME``.  It is not a field anyone briefs.
    30	
    31	``models.override`` is resolved against the speed tier rather than read
    32	literally: ``null`` means ``astra-all`` whenever ``run.speed`` is ``fast`` — in
    33	full speed mode every role, reviewers included, runs the hard model — and the
    34	published ``local/model-policy.json`` otherwise.  The literal ``"policy"`` keeps
    35	the published policy at any speed; ``"astra-all"`` forces the hard model at any
    36	speed.  ``set speed`` re-resolves it, so the tier and the models never disagree.
    37	
    38	Validation fails loudly at briefing time rather than at 05:00Z: an unknown
    39	key, a missing endpoint, a non-integer limit, ``external_reserved >=
    40	nominal_limit``, an occupancy target above 1, an unknown speed or model
    41	override, a non-positive issue number, or an account name outside
    42	``[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`` all exit 2 naming the offending key and the
    43	template path.  A missing brief is a hard error naming both paths — never
    44	silently zero and never silently unlimited capacity.
    45	
    46	**The brief seeds; the accounts file lives.**  ``apply`` writes
    47	``watchdog/accounts.json`` (``local/bin/accounts_file.py``) from the brief's
    48	``accounts`` block when that file does not exist, and **never overwrites an
    49	existing one**; where it exists it is what ``apply`` reads, so re-applying a
    50	brief to change the speed tier cannot undo the ceilings the owner has been
    51	editing all morning.  Any number of named accounts: ``primary`` and ``second``
    52	are ordinary entries, and a third key added with ``owner-tools/accounts.sh add``
    53	gets its own cap file, its own health and its own line in every report.
    54	
    55	The derived cap files ``watchdog/max-codex-<account>`` and ``max-codex`` stay
    56	where ``account_router.py``, the lane runner and ``status-snapshot.sh`` already

   250	def _require_mapping(value, key: str) -> dict:
   251	    if not isinstance(value, dict):

   256	def _require_int(value, key: str, *, minimum: int | None = None) -> int:
   257	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
   258	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} must be an integer, got {value!r}")
   259	    if minimum is not None and value < minimum:
   260	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} must be at least {minimum}, got {value}")
   261	    return value

   263	
   264	def _require_text(value, key: str, *, pattern: re.Pattern | None = None) -> str:
   265	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
   266	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} must be a non-empty string, got {value!r}")
   267	    text = value.strip()
   268	    if pattern is not None and not pattern.match(text):
   269	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} {text!r} does not match {pattern.pattern}")
   270	    return text

   273	def parse_timestamp(value, key: str) -> datetime:
   274	    """ISO-8601 instant; a bare `Z` is accepted on Python 3.10 too."""
   275	    text = _require_text(value, key)
   276	    candidate = text[:-1] + "+00:00" if text.endswith(("Z", "z")) else text
   277	    try:
   278	        moment = datetime.fromisoformat(candidate)
   279	    except ValueError as exc:
   280	        raise BriefError(key, f"{key} {text!r} is not an ISO-8601 timestamp "
   281	                              f"(e.g. 2026-09-13T04:00:00Z): {exc}") from exc
   282	    if moment.tzinfo is None:
   283	        moment = moment.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   284	    return moment.astimezone(timezone.utc)

   287	def _validate_run(run: dict) -> dict:
   288	    _require_mapping(run, "run")
   289	    unknown = sorted(set(run) - set(RUN_KEYS_REQUIRED) - set(RUN_KEYS_OPTIONAL))
   290	    if unknown:
   291	        raise BriefError(f"run.{unknown[0]}",
   292	                         f"unknown key(s) under 'run': {', '.join(unknown)}")
   293	    missing = [key for key in RUN_KEYS_REQUIRED if key not in run]
   294	    if missing:
   295	        raise BriefError(f"run.{missing[0]}",
   296	                         f"'run' is missing: {', '.join(missing)}")
   297	
   298	    out: dict = {}
   299	    out["label"] = sanitize(_require_text(run["label"], "run.label"), 120)
   300	    out["start"] = parse_timestamp(run["start"], "run.start").strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
   301	
   302	    cutoff = run["dispatch_cutoff"]
   303	    if isinstance(cutoff, str) and cutoff.strip().lower() == CUTOFF_OPEN:
   304	        out["dispatch_cutoff"] = CUTOFF_OPEN
   305	    else:
   306	        out["dispatch_cutoff"] = parse_timestamp(
   307	            cutoff, "run.dispatch_cutoff").strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
   308	        if out["dispatch_cutoff"] <= out["start"]:
   309	            raise BriefError("run.dispatch_cutoff",
   310	                             f"run.dispatch_cutoff {out['dispatch_cutoff']} is not after "
   311	                             f"run.start {out['start']}; use the literal "
   312	                             f"{CUTOFF_OPEN!r} for an open-ended run")
   313	
   314	    out["pause_deadline_min"] = _require_int(
   315	        run["pause_deadline_min"], "run.pause_deadline_min", minimum=1)
   316	
   317	    speed = run["speed"]
   318	    if speed not in SPEEDS:
   319	        raise BriefError("run.speed",
   320	                         f"run.speed must be one of {SPEEDS}, got {speed!r}")
   321	    out["speed"] = speed
   322	
   323	    target = run["occupancy_target"]
   324	    if isinstance(target, bool) or not isinstance(target, (int, float)):
   325	        raise BriefError("run.occupancy_target",
   326	                         f"run.occupancy_target must be a number, got {target!r}")
   327	    if not 0 < float(target) <= 1:
   328	        raise BriefError("run.occupancy_target",
   329	                         f"run.occupancy_target must lie in (0, 1], got {target} — "
   330	                         "it is a fraction of the effective cap, not a worker count")
   331	    out["occupancy_target"] = float(target)
   332	
   333	    for key in ISSUE_KEYS:
   334	        out[key] = _require_int(run[key], f"run.{key}", minimum=1)
   335	    if len({out[key] for key in ISSUE_KEYS}) != len(ISSUE_KEYS):
   336	        raise BriefError("run.estimate_issue",
   337	                         "the progress log, the estimate issue and the owner inbox must be "
   338	                         "three different issues; the estimate issue carries exactly two "
   339	                         "rendered lines and nothing else (issues-prs.md section 6)")
   340	
   341	    if run.get("turn_max_min") is not None:
   342	        out["turn_max_min"] = _require_int(run["turn_max_min"], "run.turn_max_min", minimum=1)
   343	    else:
   344	        out["turn_max_min"] = TURN_MAX_MIN[speed]
   345	    out["estimate_cadence_min"] = ESTIMATE_CADENCE_MIN[speed]
   346	    out["main"] = _validate_main(run.get("main"))
   347	    return out

   353	    Optional; every field defaults to what ``main-session.sh`` used to hard-code.
   354	    Validated at briefing time so a typo is an exit 2 at ``apply`` rather than a
   355	    codex CLI error at 04:00Z.

   358	        return dict(MAIN_DEFAULTS)

   361	    if unknown:
   362	        raise BriefError(f"run.main.{unknown[0]}",
   363	                         f"unknown key(s) under 'run.main': {', '.join(unknown)}")

   383	def _validate_accounts(accounts) -> list[dict]:
   384	    if not isinstance(accounts, list) or not accounts:
   385	        raise BriefError("accounts", "'accounts' must be a non-empty list of account objects")
   386	    seen: set[str] = set()
   387	    out: list[dict] = []
   388	    for index, raw in enumerate(accounts):
   389	        where = f"accounts[{index}]"
   390	        _require_mapping(raw, where)
   391	        unknown = sorted(set(raw) - set(ACCOUNT_KEYS))
   392	        if unknown:
   393	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.{unknown[0]}",
   394	                             f"unknown key(s) under {where}: {', '.join(unknown)}")
   395	        missing = [key for key in ACCOUNT_KEYS if key not in raw]
   396	        if missing:
   397	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.{missing[0]}",
   398	                             f"{where} is missing: {', '.join(missing)}")
   399	        name = _require_text(raw["name"], f"{where}.name",
   400	                             pattern=accounts_file.NAME_RE)
   401	        if name in seen:
   402	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.name", f"account {name!r} is listed twice")
   403	        seen.add(name)
   404	        endpoint = _require_text(raw["endpoint"], f"{where}.endpoint", pattern=ENDPOINT_RE)
   405	        codex_home = _require_text(raw["codex_home"], f"{where}.codex_home")
   406	        nominal = _require_int(raw["nominal_limit"], f"{where}.nominal_limit", minimum=1)
   407	        reserved = _require_int(raw["external_reserved"], f"{where}.external_reserved", minimum=0)
   408	        if reserved >= nominal:
   409	            raise BriefError(
   410	                f"{where}.external_reserved",
   411	                f"{where}: external_reserved {reserved} leaves no slot below "
   412	                f"nominal_limit {nominal}; nominal_limit is a ceiling for the whole key, "
   413	                "and the pipeline's share is nominal_limit - external_reserved")
   414	        enabled = raw["enabled"]
   415	        if not isinstance(enabled, bool):
   416	            raise BriefError(f"{where}.enabled",
   417	                             f"{where}.enabled must be true or false, got {enabled!r}")
   418	        out.append({
   419	            "name": name,
   420	            "label": sanitize(_require_text(raw["label"], f"{where}.label"), 60),

420	            "label": sanitize(_require_text(raw["label"], f"{where}.label"), 60),
   421	            "endpoint": endpoint,
   422	            "codex_home": codex_home,
   423	            "codex_home_path": str(Path(codex_home).expanduser()),
   424	            "nominal_limit": nominal,
   425	            "external_reserved": reserved,

   447	def resolve_override(speed: str, briefed: str | None) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
   448	    """The override actually in force for *speed*, and where it came from.
   449	
   450	    A briefed ``null`` resolves from the speed tier: ``fast`` is ``astra-all``,
   451	    because in full speed mode every role — reviewers included — runs the hard
   452	    model.  ``"policy"`` is how a fast run says "leave the published policy
   453	    alone"; it is deliberately a word rather than the absence of one, so the
   454	    file records a decision instead of an omission.
   455	    """
   456	    published = "published local/model-policy.json"
   457	    if briefed == "policy":
   458	        return (None, f"brief: models.override 'policy' ({published})")
   459	    if briefed is not None:
   460	        return (briefed, "brief: models.override")
   461	    resolved = SPEED_DEFAULT_OVERRIDE.get(speed)
   462	    if resolved is None:
   463	        return (None, f"default for run.speed {speed} ({published})")
   464	    return (resolved, f"default for run.speed {speed} (every role, reviewers included)")

   502	def read_brief(path: Path) -> tuple[dict, str]:
   503	    """Read, validate and digest the brief at *path*."""
   504	    if not path.exists():
   505	        raise BriefError("brief", f"no run brief at {path}\n{_template_hint()}\n"
   506	                                  "Copy the template, edit the values, then re-run "
   507	                                  "'run_mode.py apply'. A run never starts with an "
   508	                                  "assumed capacity.")
   509	    raw = path.read_bytes()
   510	    digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
   511	    try:
   512	        doc = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
   513	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   514	        raise BriefError("brief", f"{path} is not valid JSON: {exc}\n{_template_hint()}") from exc
   515	    return validate_brief(doc), digest

   551	def effective_caps(brief: dict, measured: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> dict[str, int]:
   552	    """Starting cap per account.
   553	
   554	    ``cap0 = clamp(1, nominal_limit - external_reserved,
   555	    last_measured_limit or nominal_limit - external_reserved)`` — a run starts
   556	    below the measured cliff instead of above it.  A disabled or unlisted
   557	    account is 0: the pipeline never dispatches there at all.
   558	    """
   559	    seen = measured or {}
   560	    caps = {account["name"]: 0 for account in brief["accounts"]}
   561	    for account in brief["accounts"]:
   562	        if not account["enabled"]:
   563	            continue
   564	        base = account["nominal_limit"] - account["external_reserved"]
   565	        target = base

   567	        if isinstance(limit, int) and limit >= 0:
   568	            target = min(base, limit)

   570	        # taken every slot of that key for now.  That is 0, not the floor of 1 —
   571	        # the clamp exists so a measured limit never seeds a disabled-looking
   572	        # cap, not to invent a slot the owner says is not theirs.
   573	        caps[account["name"]] = max(1, min(base, target)) if base > 0 else 0

900	def value_for(mode: dict, key: str, root: Path | None = None):
   901	    """One value for ``get KEY``; unknown keys raise ``LayerError``."""
   902	    if key in SCALAR_KEYS:
   903	        return SCALAR_KEYS[key](mode)
   904	    caps = current_caps(mode, root)
   905	    if key == "floor":
   906	        return floor_for(caps, mode["run"]["occupancy_target"])
   907	    if key == "max_codex":
   908	        return sum(caps.values())
   909	    if key == "accounts":
   910	        return " ".join(a["name"] for a in mode["accounts"] if a.get("enabled"))
   911	    if "." in key:
   912	        field, _, name = key.partition(".")
   913	        if field in PER_ACCOUNT_KEYS and name in names_of(mode):
   914	            row = account_row(mode, name)
   915	            if field == "cap":
   916	                return caps.get(name, 0)
   917	            if field == "codex_home":
   918	                return row.get("codex_home_path") or row["codex_home"]
   919	            if field == "enabled":
   920	                return "yes" if row["enabled"] else "no"
   921	            return row[field]
   922	    known = sorted(list(SCALAR_KEYS) + ["floor", "max_codex", "accounts"] +
   923	                   [f"{field}.<account>" for field in PER_ACCOUNT_KEYS])
   924	    raise LayerError(f"unknown key {key!r}; known keys: {', '.join(known)}")

  1024	def render_shim(template: str, speed: str) -> str:

  1026	    if speed not in SPEEDS:

  1029	    # anchored SPEED_ARGS= line.  Anchored at the start of the line on purpose -
  1030	    # the template's header documents both renderings, and a comment that merely
  1031	    # shows the line must never be rewritten with it.

  1036	                f"{shim_template_path()} has {len(speed_lines)} lines starting "
  1037	                "with SPEED_ARGS=; exactly one is required (install.sh renders "
  1038	                "the same line and exits 5 on the same condition).")
  1039	        return _SPEED_ARGS_RE.sub(
  1040	            lambda _match: SPEED_ARGS_LINE[speed], template, count=1)
  1041	    stripped = _SERVICE_TIER_RE.sub("", template)
  1042	    if SPEED_PLACEHOLDER in stripped:
  1043	        return _PLACEHOLDER_RE.sub(PRIORITY_ARG + " " if speed == "fast" else "", stripped)

  1046	            f"{shim_template_path()} carries neither {SPEED_PLACEHOLDER} nor the "
  1047	            f"anchor {SHIM_ANCHOR}; the speed tier has no rendering position. Fix the "
  1048	            "committed template (results/telemetry/owner-tools/owner-bin-codex) rather "
  1049	            "than hand-patching the deployed shim.")

  1055	def record_shim() -> str:
  1056	    """Re-record the regenerated shim in ``owner-bin/manifest.sha256``.
  1057	
  1058	    ``install.sh`` releases both renderings into ``manifest.accepted`` but keeps
  1059	    ``manifest.sha256`` at the deployed one, and the merge daemon's start gate is
  1060	    ``install.sh --verify``.  Without this step the first ``set speed`` of a run
  1061	    makes the daemon refuse to start.  Best effort: a missing or failing
  1062	    installer is a warning, never a reason to leave the speed change unmade.
  1063	    """
  1064	    installer = repo_root() / "results" / "telemetry" / "owner-tools" / "install.sh"
  1065	    if not installer.is_file():
  1066	        return f"manifest not re-recorded: no {installer}"
  1067	    try:
  1068	        done = subprocess.run(["bash", str(installer), "--record", "codex"],
  1069	                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
  1070	    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
  1071	        return f"warning: install.sh --record codex did not run: {exc}"
  1072	    if done.returncode != 0:
  1073	        detail = (done.stderr or done.stdout).strip().splitlines()
  1074	        return ("warning: install.sh --record codex failed: "
  1075	                + (detail[-1] if detail else f"exit {done.returncode}"))

  1079	def _shim_diff(live: str, wanted: str) -> str:
  1080	    return "".join(difflib.unified_diff(

  1085	def apply_speed(mode: dict, speed: str, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
  1086	    """Regenerate the deployed shim; refuse when it was hand-edited."""
  1087	    template_file = shim_template_path()
  1088	    try:
  1089	        template = template_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  1090	    except OSError as exc:
  1091	        raise LayerError(f"cannot read the shim template {template_file}: {exc}") from exc
  1092	    wanted = render_shim(template, speed)
  1093	    renderings = {render_shim(template, tier) for tier in SPEEDS}
  1094	    live_file = shim_path()
  1095	    try:
  1096	        live = live_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
  1097	    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
  1098	        raise Refused(
  1099	            f"no deployed shim at {live_file}; install the operator tools first "
  1100	            "(results/telemetry/owner-tools/install.sh)") from exc
  1101	    if live not in renderings:
  1102	        raise Refused(
  1103	            f"the deployed shim {live_file} differs from every rendering of "
  1104	            f"{template_file}; refusing to discard an emergency hand-edit.\n"
  1105	            "Fold the edit into the committed template, redeploy, then retry.\n"
  1106	            + _shim_diff(live, wanted))
  1107	    if dry_run:
  1108	        return "dry-run: shim unchanged"
  1109	    if live == wanted:
  1110	        return f"shim already at {speed} speed"
  1111	    mode_bits = os.stat(live_file).st_mode & 0o777
  1112	    atomic_write(live_file, wanted)
  1113	    os.chmod(live_file, mode_bits or 0o755)
  1114	    return f"shim regenerated at {speed} speed; {record_shim()}"

  1121	def locked_append(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
  1122	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1123	    fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
  1124	    with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
  1125	        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
  1126	        try:
  1127	            handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1128	            if handle.tell():
  1129	                handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)
  1130	                if handle.read(1) != "\n":
  1131	                    handle.write("\n")
  1132	                handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
  1133	            handle.write(text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n")
  1134	            handle.flush()
  1135	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
  1136	        finally:
  1137	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

 def read_brief(path: Path) -> tuple[dict, str]:
     """Read, validate and digest the brief at *path*."""
     if not path.exists():
         raise BriefError("brief", f"no run brief at {path}\n{_template_hint()}\n"
                                   "Copy the template, edit the values, then re-run "
                                   "'run_mode.py apply'. A run never starts with an "
                                   "assumed capacity.")
     raw = path.read_bytes()
     digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
     try:
         doc = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
     except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
         raise BriefError("brief", f"{path} is not valid JSON: {exc}\n{_template_hint()}") from exc
     return validate_brief(doc), digest

     Validating the field and exposing it through ``get model_override`` is not

     """`both` when more than one account is enabled, `primary` otherwise.
 
     DERIVED, never briefed.  The shim's `primary-only policy` check was a second
     file holding a capacity decision: with the file absent it defaults to
     `primary`, and every dispatch whose CODEX_HOME is not ~/.codex exits 4.  So a

     lives (full-speed-mode.md section 1: every number the owner states lives in
     exactly one file), and this function is the only thing that derives the file

                caps: dict[str, int], measured: dict[str, int]) -> dict:

         row["measured_limit"] = measured.get(account["name"])

     ``manifest.sha256`` at the deployed one, and the merge daemon's start gate is

     try:

                               capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
     except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
         return f"warning: install.sh --record codex did not run: {exc}"

         detail = (done.stderr or done.stdout).strip().splitlines()
         return ("warning: install.sh --record codex failed: "

     return "manifest re-recorded (install.sh --record codex)"

 def locked_append(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
     path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
     fd = os.open(path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o644)
     with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
         fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
         try:
             handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
             if handle.tell():
                 handle.seek(handle.tell() - 1)
                 if handle.read(1) != "\n":
                     handle.write("\n")
                 handle.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
             handle.write(text if text.endswith("\n") else text + "\n")
             handle.flush()
             os.fsync(handle.fileno())
         finally:
             fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

 def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
         prog="run_mode.py", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0],
         formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
     parser.add_argument("--repo-root", help="checkout holding results/telemetry "
                                             "(default: this script's checkout)")
     sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
 
     p = sub.add_parser("apply", help="validate the brief and write the mode file")
     p.add_argument("--brief", help=f"default {'<cache>/watchdog/run-brief.json'}")
     p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="print the plan, write nothing")
 
     p = sub.add_parser("show", help="human-readable dump of the run mode")
     p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")
     p.add_argument("--oneline", action="store_true",
                    help="the whole mode on one line (goal text, resume message)")
 
     p = sub.add_parser("get", help="one value on stdout")
     p.add_argument("key")
 
     p = sub.add_parser("set", help="change one mid-run knob")
     p.add_argument("knob", choices=("speed",))
     p.add_argument("value")
     p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
 
     p = sub.add_parser("pause", help="stop admission: caps to 0, pre-pause caps saved")
     p.add_argument("--reason", default="")
 
     sub.add_parser("resume", help="restore the saved caps")
     return parser
 
 
 def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
     args = build_parser().parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
     if args.repo_root:
         os.environ["MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT"] = args.repo_root
     handlers = {"apply": cmd_apply, "show": cmd_show, "get": cmd_get,
                 "set": cmd_set, "pause": cmd_pause, "resume": cmd_resume}
     try:
         return handlers[args.cmd](args)
     except BriefError as exc:
         sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: invalid brief at {exc.key}: {exc}\n")
         if _template_hint() not in str(exc):
             sys.stderr.write(f"{_template_hint()}\n")
         return 2
     except Refused as exc:
         sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: refused: {exc}\n")
         return 3
     except LayerError as exc:
         sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: {exc}\n")
         return 2
     except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
         # A hand-edited run-mode.json is unknown, not zero: say so and stop.
         sys.stderr.write(f"run_mode.py: {mode_path()} is incomplete ({exc!r}); "
                          "re-run 'run_mode.py apply'. Treat the run mode as "
                          "unknown, never as zero capacity.\n")
         return 2
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     raise SystemExit(main())

+class TestInvalidAccountsFile(RunModeTestCase):
+    """A typo in the file the owner is invited to hand-edit must not break the
+    pause.  `owner-pause.sh` phase T+0:00 is `run_mode.py pause`; when that
+    exited 2, admission was never stopped, the pre-pause caps were never saved,
+    and the whole script exited 3 — while the GitHub channel, the one remote
+    repair path for that very file, was dead for the same reason."""
+
+    def break_accounts(self) -> None:
+        path = self.cache / "watchdog" / "accounts.json"
+        document = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        document["accounts"][0]["cieling"] = 5      # the owner's typo
+        path.write_text(json.dumps(document), encoding="utf-8")
+
+    def test_pause_still_zeroes_and_saves_the_caps(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(run(["apply"])[0], 0)
+        self.break_accounts()
+        code, _, err = run(["pause", "--reason", "owner word"])
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertIn("WARNING", err)
+        self.assertIn("cieling", err)
+        self.assertEqual((self.cap("max-codex-primary"), self.cap("max-codex-second"),
+                          self.cap("max-codex")), ("0", "0", "0"))
+        self.assertEqual(self.mode()["saved_caps"], {"primary": 5, "second": 28})
+
+    def test_resume_still_restores_the_saved_caps(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(run(["apply"])[0], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(run(["pause"])[0], 0)
+        self.break_accounts()
+        self.assertEqual(run(["resume"])[0], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(self.cap("max-codex-primary"), "5")
+
+    def test_a_run_scalar_is_still_answerable(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual(run(["apply"])[0], 0)
+        expected = run(["get", "owner_inbox_issue"])[1].strip()
+        self.break_accounts()
+        code, out, err = run(["get", "owner_inbox_issue"])
+        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
+        self.assertEqual(out.strip(), expected)
+        self.assertIn("WARNING", err)
+
+    def test_a_ceiling_question_still_fails_hard(self) -> None:
+        # These would ACT on a ceiling, so answering from the briefed snapshot
+        # would restore a number the owner had just lowered.
+        self.assertEqual(run(["apply"])[0], 0)
+        self.break_accounts()
+        for key in ("cap.primary", "nominal_limit.second", "floor", "max_codex",
+                    "accounts", "account_mode"):
+            self.assertEqual(run(["get", key])[0], 2, key)

   473	class TestInvalidAccountsFile(RunModeTestCase):

   475	    pause.  `owner-pause.sh` phase T+0:00 is `run_mode.py pause`; when that
   476	    exited 2, admission was never stopped, the pre-pause caps were never saved,
   477	    and the whole script exited 3 — while the GitHub channel, the one remote
   478	    repair path for that very file, was dead for the same reason."""

   480	    def break_accounts(self) -> None:
   481	        path = self.cache / "watchdog" / "accounts.json"
   482	        document = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

A configuration with only `second` or `third` enabled is therefore admitted by the router but rejected by the deployed shim; I’m checking the dispatcher and health-classification paths next for similar identity mismatches.

   798	valid_label() {
   799	  # [a-z0-9.-]{1,40}.  A label travels into a JSON record and into log lines; it
   800	  # is never interpolated into a command or a path unquoted, and one outside the
   801	  # class fails closed rather than being rewritten to `unknown` — the rewrite is
   802	  # what hid which key a failure belonged to on 2026-09-12.
   803	  local value="$1"
   804	  [ -n "$value" ] || return 1
   805	  [ "${#value}" -le 40 ] || return 1
   806	  case "$value" in
   807	    *[!a-z0-9.-]*) return 1 ;;
   808	  esac
   809	  return 0
   810	}

   812	run_mode_field() {
   813	  # run_mode_field <dotted.key> — one scalar from the run mode file, or empty.
   814	  # `run_mode.py get` (work item W1) is the single accessor when it is present;
   815	  # the mode file is read directly otherwise, so this script does not depend on
   816	  # the landing order of the two changes and works with neither.
   817	  local key="$1" value=""
   818	  if [ -f "$RUN_MODE_PY" ]; then
   819	    value="$(python3 "$RUN_MODE_PY" get "$key" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   820	  fi
   821	  if [ -n "$value" ]; then
   822	    printf '%s' "$value"
   823	    return 0
   824	  fi
   825	  [ -f "$RUN_MODE_JSON" ] || return 0
   826	  python3 - "$RUN_MODE_JSON" "$key" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null || true
   827	import json, sys

   829	try:
   830	    data = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8"))
   831	except Exception:
   832	    raise SystemExit(0)

   834	for part in sys.argv[2].split("."):
   835	    if isinstance(node, dict) and part in node:
   836	        node = node[part]
   837	    elif isinstance(node, dict) and isinstance(node.get("run"), dict) and part in node["run"]:
   838	        node = node["run"][part]

   840	        raise SystemExit(0)

   842	    print(node)

   869	  # watchdog/accounts.json DIRECTLY — the same file `account_names()` admits
   870	  # against.  Asking `run_mode.py get codex_home.<account>` instead was the
   871	  # fail-open hole: that accessor goes through load_mode() -> with_live_accounts()

   873	  # key while the router happily admitted to it from the max-codex-* glob, and

   876	  # MIPSTARRE_CODEX_HOME_SECOND, so the historical pair still resolves with no

   904	  # These are the owner's brief as run-mode recorded it, so a key moved between
   905	  # homes keeps the identity failures and health are attributed to.

   912	except Exception:

   916	    accounts = data["run"].get("accounts")

  1087	retry_is_safe() {
  1088	  # A transient CLASS is not by itself a licence to re-run the prompt.
  1089	  # `refused`, `endpoint_down`, `concurrency_limit` and `endpoint_5xx` are
  1090	  # admission failures: the model never ran, the worktree was never touched, and
  1091	  # a retry is a pure re-attempt.  `retries_exhausted` is different — the client
  1092	  # gave up reconnecting, which can happen twenty minutes in, and re-running the
  1093	  # same prompt from scratch in a worktree that now holds the dead session's
  1094	  # partial, uncommitted edits is not a retry, it is a second worker on a dirty
  1095	  # tree.  review.sh already draws this line (ended-started < 15 s, tokens 0);
  1096	  # draw the same one here: retry only a death that did no work and left a clean
  1097	  # tree.  Anything else is left to the janitor's dead-session pass, which
  1098	  # re-dispatches under a per-(pr, role, head) budget with the state in hand.
  1099	  local dirty=""
  1100	  case "$FAILURE_CLASS" in retries_exhausted) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
  1101	  case "${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL:-0}" in
  1102	    ''|0) ;;
  1103	    *) note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': the session used ${DISPATCH_USAGE_TOTAL} tokens \
  1104	before dying, so a re-run would repeat work in a tree that holds its partial edits"
  1105	       return 1 ;;
  1106	  esac
  1107	  if [ -n "${WORKTREE_ABS:-}" ]; then
  1108	    dirty="$(git -C "$WORKTREE_ABS" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^?? ' || true)"
  1109	  fi
  1110	  if [ -n "$dirty" ]; then
  1110	  if [ -n "$dirty" ]; then
  1111	    note "not retrying '$FAILURE_CLASS': $WORKTREE_ABS has uncommitted changes from the \
  1112	dead session; the janitor's dead-session pass owns this one"
  1113	    return 1
  1114	  fi
  1115	  return 0
  1116	}

  1118	backoff_or_give_up() {
  1119	  # Jittered exponential backoff, base 30 s and cap 10 min. Returns 0 to retry.
  1120	  local exponent delay jitter total
  1121	  if [ "$ATTEMPT" -ge "$MAX_ATTEMPTS" ]; then
  1122	    note "attempt $ATTEMPT of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; no attempt left"
  1123	    return 1
  1124	  fi
  1125	  if cutoff_passed; then
  1126	    note "the run's dispatch cutoff has passed; not retrying after '$FAILURE_CLASS'"
  1127	    return 1
  1128	  fi
  1129	  exponent=$((ATTEMPT - 1))
  1130	  [ "$exponent" -le 20 ] || exponent=20
  1131	  delay=$((BACKOFF_BASE_S * (1 << exponent)))
  1132	  [ "$delay" -le "$BACKOFF_MAX_S" ] || delay="$BACKOFF_MAX_S"
  1133	  jitter=$((RANDOM % (delay / 2 + 1)))
  1134	  total=$((delay + jitter))
  1135	  ATTEMPT=$((ATTEMPT + 1))
  1136	  write_spool retrying
  1137	  note "attempt $((ATTEMPT - 1)) of $MAX_ATTEMPTS ended '$FAILURE_CLASS'; \
  1138	retrying as attempt $ATTEMPT in ${total}s"
  1139	  sleep "$total"
  1140	  if cutoff_passed; then
  1141	    note "the run's dispatch cutoff passed during the backoff; stopping"
  1142	    return 1
  1143	  fi
  1144	  return 0
  1145	}

  1147	report_and_exit_refused() {
  1148	  # One `refused` row for the whole episode, then exit 7 with the spool intact.
  1149	  # `refused` is not `failed`: the dispatch was never admitted, so it must not
  1150	  # be scored as a failed attempt against a proof packet's budget.
  1151	  local ts
  1152	  ts="$(date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z)"
  1153	  if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]; then
  1154	    printf '%s\n' "{\"type\":\"dispatch.refused\",\"failure_class\":\"$FAILURE_CLASS\",\
  1155	\"attempts\":$ATTEMPT,\"account\":\"$ACCOUNT_REQUESTED\",\"endpoint\":\"$ENDPOINT_LABEL\",\
  1156	\"ts\":\"$ts\"}" >"$CAPTURE"
  1157	    cp "$CAPTURE" "$PUBLISHED_CAPTURE_DIR/$NAME.jsonl" 2>/dev/null ||
  1158	      note "warning: could not copy the refusal record into $PUBLISHED_CAPTURE_DIR"
  1159	    REFUSED_ARGS=(--repo-root "$REPO_ROOT" session-summarize
  1160	      "$PUBLISHED_CAPTURE_DIR/$NAME.jsonl" --name "$NAME" --role "$ROLE" --issue "$ISSUE"
  1161	      --start "$START_TS" --end "$ts" --dispatcher "$DISPATCHER" --worktree "$WORKTREE_ABS"
  1162	      --status refused --failure-class "$FAILURE_CLASS" --key-label "$KEY_LABEL"
  1163	      --endpoint "$ENDPOINT_LABEL" --no-rollout-scan --append-to "$REGISTRY")
  1164	    [ -z "$PR_ID" ] || REFUSED_ARGS+=(--pr "$PR_ID")
  1165	    python3 "$TELEMETRY_PY" "${REFUSED_ARGS[@]}" >/dev/null ||
  1166	      note "warning: could not record the refusal for $NAME; the capture is at $CAPTURE"
  1167	  fi
  1168	  printf 'name: %s\n' "$NAME"
  1169	  printf 'account: %s\n' "$ACCOUNT_REQUESTED"
  1170	  printf 'endpoint: %s\n' "$ENDPOINT_LABEL"
  1171	  printf 'failure_class: %s\n' "$FAILURE_CLASS"
  1172	  printf 'attempts: %s\n' "$ATTEMPT"
  1173	  printf 'spool: %s\n' "${SPOOL_FILE:-none}"
  1174	  printf 'exit: 7\n'
  1175	  note "not admitted after $ATTEMPT attempt(s) ('$FAILURE_CLASS'); \
  1176	the spool entry is left for the janitor"
  1177	  exit 7
  1178	}

   719	def append_session_record(registry: Path, record: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
   720	    """Append a registry line unless an identical observation is already there.
   721	
   722	    The registry is append-only (meta.md, "Two memory disciplines"): a later
   723	    line supersedes an earlier one for the same ``name``.  Idempotency is
   724	    therefore keyed on (name, status, thread_id, exit) so that re-running a
   725	    summarize over the same capture does not duplicate a line, while a genuine
   726	    status transition still appends.
   727	    """
   728	    registry.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   729	    fd = os.open(registry, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
   730	    with os.fdopen(fd, "r+", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   731	        fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   732	        try:
   733	            handle.seek(0)
   734	            for raw in handle.read().splitlines():
   735	                raw = raw.strip()
   736	                if not raw:
   737	                    continue
   738	                try:
   739	                    existing = json.loads(raw)
   740	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
   741	                    continue
   742	                if not isinstance(existing, dict):
   743	                    continue
   744	                if (
   745	                    existing.get("name") == record.get("name")
   746	                    and existing.get("status") == record.get("status")
   747	                    and existing.get("thread_id") == record.get("thread_id")
   748	                    and existing.get("exit") == record.get("exit")
   749	                    and (record.get('dispatcher') != 'native' or existing == record)
   750	                ):
   751	                    return False
   752	            _ensure_trailing_newline(handle)
   753	            handle.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
   754	            handle.flush()
   755	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
   756	            return True
   757	        finally:
   758	            fcntl.flock(handle.fileno(), fcntl.LOCK_UN)

   803	def event_session_label(raw: str | None = None) -> str:
   804	    """Filename-safe shard label for the writing session.
   805	
   806	    Two sessions must never touch one path: that is the whole point of the
   807	    shard.  The label is the dispatching session name (``MIPSTARRE_SESSION``)
   808	    reduced to ``[A-Za-z0-9._-]``; an unnamed writer gets ``unknown``, and
   809	    concurrent unnamed writers still serialize on the per-path lock below.
   810	    """
   811	    value = raw if raw is not None else os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_SESSION", "")
   812	    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", (value or "").strip()).strip("-.")
   813	    return cleaned[:60] or "unknown"

   821	def append_event_bullet(
   822	    path: Path, text: str, date_str: str, header: str = EVENTS_HEADER
   823	) -> str:
   824	    """Append a dated bullet, creating today's ``## YYYY-MM-DD`` section."""
   825	    bullet_lines = sanitize_text(text, limit=8000).split("\n")
   826	    bullet = "- " + bullet_lines[0]
   827	    for continuation in bullet_lines[1:]:
   828	        bullet += "\n  " + continuation.strip()
   829	    heading = f"## {date_str}"
   830	    # The lock is per path: sharded writers never contend, and two writers that
   831	    # do share a path (two unnamed callers) still cannot interleave a bullet.
   832	    with named_lock("events-" + re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", path.name)):
   833	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   834	        original = (
   835	            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if path.exists() else header
   836	        )
   837	        lines = original.splitlines()
   838	        try:
   839	            head_index = lines.index(heading)
   840	        except ValueError:
   841	            head_index = -1
   842	        if head_index < 0:
   843	            while lines and not lines[-1].strip():
   844	                lines.pop()
   845	            lines.extend(["", heading, "", bullet])
   846	        else:
   847	            end = len(lines)
   848	            for index in range(head_index + 1, len(lines)):
   849	                if lines[index].startswith("## "):
   850	                    end = index
   851	                    break
   852	            while end > head_index + 1 and not lines[end - 1].strip():
   853	                end -= 1
   854	            lines.insert(end, bullet)
   855	        _atomic_write(path, "\n".join(lines) + "\n")
   856	    return bullet

   859	DATE_HEADING_RE = re.compile(r"^##\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})")

   862	def read_event_sections(path: Path) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
   863	    """Split a log file into ``(date, heading, body)`` sections.
   864	
   865	    Historical headings carry a title or a timestamp after the date
   866	    (``## 2026-09-12T06:38:22Z - Recover primary failures``); only the leading
   867	    date is parsed, and anything before the first dated heading is ignored.
   868	    """
   869	    if not path.exists():
   870	        return []
   871	    sections: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
   872	    current_date = ""
   873	    current_heading = ""
   874	    body: list[str] = []
   875	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
   876	        match = DATE_HEADING_RE.match(line)
   877	        if match:
   878	            if current_date:
   879	                sections.append((current_date, current_heading, "\n".join(body).strip("\n")))
   880	            current_date, current_heading, body = match.group(1), line, []
   881	            continue
   882	        if current_date:
   883	            body.append(line)
   884	    if current_date:
   885	        sections.append((current_date, current_heading, "\n".join(body).strip("\n")))
   886	    return sections

item.text: The failure classifier has a more serious control-loop hazard: it scans every serialized event before considering `exit_code`. A successful session whose task or answer contains `401 Unauthorized` is recorded as `auth`, and the controller’s new threshold of one then disables that key. I’m validating the inbox’s exactly-once semantics and malformed-file recovery claim before consolidating findings.

     2	"""The owner's GitHub control channel for the live accounts file.
     3	
     4	The shell is not always at hand.  A comment on the owner inbox issue in the
     5	fixed form::
     6	
     7	    ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20
     8	    ACCOUNTS: third enabled=false
     9	
    10	is applied to ``watchdog/accounts.json`` by the janitor at its next sweep and
    11	answered with one reply saying exactly what took effect::
    12	
    13	    applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20
    14	    rejected: ACCOUNTS: fourth ceiling=10 — no account named 'fourth'; the file
    15	    has primary, second, third
    16	
    17	Three rules make this safe enough to be a control channel rather than a
    18	conversation:
    19	
    20	* **The author must be the repository owner.**  The login is taken from
    21	  ``MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN``, then from the ``Repository owner login:`` line in
    22	  ``local/README.md``, then from the owner half of the repository slug.  A
    23	  directive from anyone else is never applied; it is answered with a
    24	  ``rejected:`` line naming the author, so an attempt is visible rather than
    25	  silent.
    26	* **One reply per comment, and applying is once.**  Each answered comment gets a
    27	  reply carrying ``<!-- mipstarre-accounts comment=<id> -->``; a comment that
    28	  already has one is skipped entirely, so a sweep every minute does not re-apply
    29	  a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell.
    30	* **The channel carries ceilings, reserved slots, the enabled flag and a note —
    31	  nothing else.**  An endpoint or a codex home is a path on the owner's host and
    32	  is set with ``owner-tools/accounts.sh``, where a typo cannot travel through a
    33	  public comment.  ``accounts_file.py`` owns the parsing and the validation, so
    34	  this channel and the CLI cannot disagree about what a valid entry is.
    35	
    36	Comment bodies are untrusted text (``local/protocols/issues-prs.md`` §4): only
    37	lines matching ``ACCOUNTS:`` are read at all, every value is validated before
    38	anything is written, and nothing is ever interpolated into a shell.

    40	Usage::

    42	    accounts_inbox.py [--issue N] [--dry-run] [--limit N]
    43	
    44	Exit codes: 0 (including "nothing to do"), 2 a GitHub or run-mode failure.

    93	def owner_login(repo_root: Path | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:
    94	    """``(login, where it came from)``.  Never guesses an empty string."""
    95	    override = (os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN") or "").strip()
    96	    if override:
    97	        return override, "MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN"
    98	    readme = (repo_root or run_mode.repo_root()) / "local" / "README.md"
    99	    try:
   100	        match = OWNER_LINE_RE.search(readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   101	    except OSError:
   102	        match = None
   103	    if match:
   104	        return match.group(1), f"{readme} (Repository owner login:)"
   105	    slug = gh_common.repo_slug()
   106	    return slug.split("/")[0], f"the owner half of the repository slug {slug}"

   109	def comment_age_min(row: dict, now: datetime | None = None) -> float | None:
   110	    """Age of a comment in minutes from its ``created_at``; ``None`` when absent.
   111	
   112	    ``None`` — no timestamp, or one that does not parse — is treated as NOT
   113	    stale by `sweep`.  The REST API always supplies ``created_at``, so a missing
   114	    one means an unusual payload rather than an old comment, and refusing to
   115	    answer it would silently drop a directive the owner did write.
   116	    """
   117	    raw = row.get("created_at")
   118	    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
   119	        return None
   120	    try:
   121	        moment = datetime.fromisoformat(raw.strip().replace("Z", "+00:00"))
   122	    except ValueError:
   123	        return None
   124	    if moment.tzinfo is None:
   125	        moment = moment.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   126	    return ((now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)) - moment).total_seconds() / 60.0

   138	#: The local half of "applying is once".  The reply marker lives on GitHub and is
   139	#: written AFTER the accounts file; if that POST fails (rate limit, network, a
   140	#: `LayerError`) the edit is on disk with nothing recording it, and the next
   141	#: sweep re-applies the same directive — reverting any `accounts.sh set` the
   142	#: owner made in between.  This file is written BEFORE the edit, so the failure
   143	#: mode is "applied once, unanswered" (the owner repeats it) instead of "applied
   144	#: again and again".

   146	LEDGER_KEEP = 500

   149	def ledger_path(root: Path | None = None) -> Path:
   150	    return (root or accounts_file.cache_root()) / LEDGER_REL

   153	def applied_ids(root: Path | None = None) -> list[int]:
   154	    try:
   155	        document = json.loads(ledger_path(root).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   156	    except (OSError, ValueError):

   159	            if isinstance(value, int)] if isinstance(document, dict) else []

   162	def record_applied(comment_id: int, root: Path | None = None) -> None:
   163	    """Note the id before the file is written; never fatal, never a duplicate."""
   164	    path = ledger_path(root)
   165	    ids = applied_ids(root)
   166	    if comment_id in ids:
   167	        return
   168	    ids = (ids + [comment_id])[-LEDGER_KEEP:]
   169	    try:
   170	        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   171	        path.write_text(json.dumps({"schema": f"{MARKER}-ledger/1", "applied": ids},
   172	                                   indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
   173	    except OSError as exc:
   174	        sys.stderr.write(f"accounts_inbox.py: warning: cannot record {comment_id} "
   175	                         f"in {path}: {exc}; a failed reply could re-apply it\n")

   178	def render_reply(comment_id: int, author: str, results: list[str]) -> str:
   179	    """The owner-facing answer: what was applied, or why it was not."""
   180	    lines = [f"Accounts directive from @{sanitize(author, 40)} "
   181	             f"(comment {comment_id}):", ""]
   182	    lines += [f"- {line}" for line in results]
   183	    lines += ["",
   184	              "<sub>local/bin/accounts_inbox.py, applied to "
   185	              f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()} by local/bin/janitor.sh. "
   186	              "Form: `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] "
   187	              "[enabled=true|false]`, one per line. The live file is the source of "
   188	              "truth for admission; the capacity controller re-reads it every "
   189	              "tick.</sub>"]
   190	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
