   193	def sweep(issue: int, *, dry_run: bool = False, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
   194	          max_age_min: int = DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MIN,
   195	          now: datetime | None = None) -> list[str]:
   196	    """Answer every unanswered, recent ``ACCOUNTS:`` comment; the report lines.
   197	
   198	    Two bounds, both necessary: `limit` caps how far back the scan goes, and
   199	    `max_age_min` caps how old a directive may be and still be acted on.  A
   200	    stale one is reported in the janitor's line and NOT replied to, so the
   201	    owner's "no reply means it was not applied" rule still holds and a repeat
   202	    comment is answered normally.
   203	    """
   204	    login, source = owner_login()
   205	    comments = gh_common.api(f"issues/{issue}/comments", paginate=True) or []
   206	    applied = set(applied_ids())
   207	    report: list[str] = []
   208	    for row in comments[-limit:]:
   209	        body = row.get("body") or ""
   210	        if MARKER in body:  # one of our own replies
   211	            continue
   212	        directives = accounts_file.parse_directives(body)
   213	        if not directives:
   214	            continue
   215	        comment_id = int(row.get("id") or 0)
   216	        if not comment_id or already_answered(comments, comment_id):
   217	            continue
   218	        if comment_id in applied:
   219	            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} was already "
   220	                          "applied but its reply did not post; not applying it again")
   221	            continue
   222	        age = comment_age_min(row, now)
   223	        if max_age_min > 0 and age is not None and age > max_age_min:
   224	            report.append(
   225	                f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} is {age:.0f} min old "
   226	                f"(bound {max_age_min} min); NOT applied and not answered — capacity "
   227	                "advice this old is worse than none. Repeat it to apply it.")
   228	            continue
   229	        author = str((row.get("user") or {}).get("login") or "")
   230	        if author != login:
   231	            # Reported, never replied to.  A public reply echoing a stranger's
   232	            # text back let anyone with comment access make the bot comment once
   233	            # per comment they wrote.  The author check is the load-bearing part
   234	            # and is unchanged; the attempt is still visible, in the janitor's
   235	            # own report, where the owner reads it.
   236	            report += [
   237	                f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} by "
   238	                f"@{sanitize(author, 40) or 'an unknown account'}: ignored — this "
   239	                f"channel applies only the repository owner's comments ({login}, "
   240	                f"from {source}); {record['raw']}"
   241	                for record in directives]
   242	            continue
   243	        if dry_run:
   244	            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: comment {comment_id} by @{author}: "
   245	                          f"{len(directives)} directive(s) would be applied (dry run)")
   246	            continue
   247	        record_applied(comment_id)
   248	        results = accounts_file.apply_directives(
   249	            body, actor=f"github:{author}", origin=f"#{issue} comment {comment_id}")
   250	        gh_common.ensure_pr_comment(issue, reply_marker(comment_id),
   251	                                    render_reply(comment_id, author, results))
   252	        for line in results:
   253	            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} "
   254	                          f"by @{author}: {line}")
   255	    if not report:
   256	        report.append("accounts-inbox: no new ACCOUNTS: directive")
   257	    return report

@@ -0,0 +1,297 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""The owner's GitHub control channel for the live accounts file.
+
+The shell is not always at hand.  A comment on the owner inbox issue in the
+fixed form::
+
+    ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20
+    ACCOUNTS: third enabled=false
+
+is applied to ``watchdog/accounts.json`` by the janitor at its next sweep and
+answered with one reply saying exactly what took effect::
+
+    applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20
+    rejected: ACCOUNTS: fourth ceiling=10 — no account named 'fourth'; the file
+    has primary, second, third
+
+Three rules make this safe enough to be a control channel rather than a
+conversation:
+
+* **The author must be the repository owner.**  The login is taken from
+  ``MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN``, then from the ``Repository owner login:`` line in
+  ``local/README.md``, then from the owner half of the repository slug.  A
+  directive from anyone else is never applied; it is answered with a
+  ``rejected:`` line naming the author, so an attempt is visible rather than
+  silent.
+* **One reply per comment, and applying is once.**  Each answered comment gets a
+  reply carrying ``<!-- mipstarre-accounts comment=<id> -->``; a comment that
+  already has one is skipped entirely, so a sweep every minute does not re-apply
+  a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell.
+* **The channel carries ceilings, reserved slots, the enabled flag and a note —
+  nothing else.**  An endpoint or a codex home is a path on the owner's host and
+  is set with ``owner-tools/accounts.sh``, where a typo cannot travel through a
+  public comment.  ``accounts_file.py`` owns the parsing and the validation, so
+  this channel and the CLI cannot disagree about what a valid entry is.
+
+Comment bodies are untrusted text (``local/protocols/issues-prs.md`` §4): only
+lines matching ``ACCOUNTS:`` are read at all, every value is validated before
+anything is written, and nothing is ever interpolated into a shell.
+
+Usage::
+
+    accounts_inbox.py [--issue N] [--dry-run] [--limit N]
+
+Exit codes: 0 (including "nothing to do"), 2 a GitHub or run-mode failure.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import re
+import sys
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
+try:
+    import gh_common
+except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
+    sys.stderr.write(f"accounts_inbox.py: cannot import gh_common.py ({exc}).\n")
+    raise SystemExit(2)
+
+import accounts_file  # noqa: E402
+import run_mode  # noqa: E402
+from wf_util import LayerError, sanitize  # noqa: E402
+
+MARKER = "mipstarre-accounts"
+
+#: The line ``local/README.md`` carries, and the only thing read from it.
+OWNER_LINE_RE = re.compile(
+    r"Repository owner login:\s*\**\s*`?([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,38})`?")
+
+#: How many of the newest comments are looked at at all.  A COUNT bound only;
+#: the temporal bound below is the one the staleness rule needs.
+DEFAULT_LIMIT = 40
+
+#: Comments older than this are not answered.  A directive the janitor never saw
+#: — the daemon was down for a day — is stale capacity advice, and applying it
+#: hours later would be worse than ignoring it.  The count cap alone did not
+#: implement that rule: the owner inbox issue is permissions-only and low
+#: traffic, so far fewer than `DEFAULT_LIMIT` comments exist and every
+#: `ACCOUNTS:` comment ever written stayed in scope forever.  With the pipeline
+#: deliberately paused, the janitor's first sweep after a resume would have
+#: applied the whole backlog at once — including `enabled=false`, which is cap 0
+#: and no probe — silently overriding the brief just applied.  Several janitor
+#: sweeps wide (daemon.conf `janitor_interval_s` defaults to 900 s), so a
+#: directive written while the daemon was briefly down still lands.  The owner
+#: sees no reply and can repeat it; ``--max-age-min 0`` turns the bound off.
+DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MIN = 120
+
+
+def owner_login(repo_root: Path | None = None) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """``(login, where it came from)``.  Never guesses an empty string."""
+    override = (os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN") or "").strip()
+    if override:
+        return override, "MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN"
+    readme = (repo_root or run_mode.repo_root()) / "local" / "README.md"
+    try:
+        match = OWNER_LINE_RE.search(readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except OSError:
+        match = None
+    if match:
+        return match.group(1), f"{readme} (Repository owner login:)"
+    slug = gh_common.repo_slug()
+    return slug.split("/")[0], f"the owner half of the repository slug {slug}"
+
+
+def comment_age_min(row: dict, now: datetime | None = None) -> float | None:
+    """Age of a comment in minutes from its ``created_at``; ``None`` when absent.
+
+    ``None`` — no timestamp, or one that does not parse — is treated as NOT
+    stale by `sweep`.  The REST API always supplies ``created_at``, so a missing
+    one means an unusual payload rather than an old comment, and refusing to
+    answer it would silently drop a directive the owner did write.
+    """
+    raw = row.get("created_at")
+    if not isinstance(raw, str) or not raw.strip():
+        return None
+    try:
+        moment = datetime.fromisoformat(raw.strip().replace("Z", "+00:00"))
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+    if moment.tzinfo is None:
+        moment = moment.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
+    return ((now or datetime.now(timezone.utc)) - moment).total_seconds() / 60.0
+
+
+def reply_marker(comment_id: int) -> str:
+    return f"<!-- {MARKER} comment={comment_id} -->"
+
+
+def already_answered(comments: list[dict], comment_id: int) -> bool:
+    marker = reply_marker(comment_id)
+    return any(marker in (row.get("body") or "") for row in comments)
+
+
+#: The local half of "applying is once".  The reply marker lives on GitHub and is
+#: written AFTER the accounts file; if that POST fails (rate limit, network, a
+#: `LayerError`) the edit is on disk with nothing recording it, and the next
+#: sweep re-applies the same directive — reverting any `accounts.sh set` the
+#: owner made in between.  This file is written BEFORE the edit, so the failure
+#: mode is "applied once, unanswered" (the owner repeats it) instead of "applied
+#: again and again".
+LEDGER_REL = Path("watchdog") / "capacity" / "inbox-applied.json"
+LEDGER_KEEP = 500
+
+
+def ledger_path(root: Path | None = None) -> Path:
+    return (root or accounts_file.cache_root()) / LEDGER_REL
+
+
+def applied_ids(root: Path | None = None) -> list[int]:
+    try:
+        document = json.loads(ledger_path(root).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    except (OSError, ValueError):
+        return []
+    return [int(value) for value in document.get("applied", [])
+            if isinstance(value, int)] if isinstance(document, dict) else []
+
+
+def record_applied(comment_id: int, root: Path | None = None) -> None:
+    """Note the id before the file is written; never fatal, never a duplicate."""
+    path = ledger_path(root)
+    ids = applied_ids(root)
+    if comment_id in ids:
+        return
+    ids = (ids + [comment_id])[-LEDGER_KEEP:]
+    try:
+        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        path.write_text(json.dumps({"schema": f"{MARKER}-ledger/1", "applied": ids},
+                                   indent=1) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    except OSError as exc:
+        sys.stderr.write(f"accounts_inbox.py: warning: cannot record {comment_id} "
+                         f"in {path}: {exc}; a failed reply could re-apply it\n")
+
+
+def render_reply(comment_id: int, author: str, results: list[str]) -> str:
+    """The owner-facing answer: what was applied, or why it was not."""
+    lines = [f"Accounts directive from @{sanitize(author, 40)} "
+             f"(comment {comment_id}):", ""]
+    lines += [f"- {line}" for line in results]
+    lines += ["",
+              "<sub>local/bin/accounts_inbox.py, applied to "
+              f"{accounts_file.accounts_path()} by local/bin/janitor.sh. "
+              "Form: `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] "
+              "[enabled=true|false]`, one per line. The live file is the source of "
+              "truth for admission; the capacity controller re-reads it every "
+              "tick.</sub>"]
+    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
+
+
+def sweep(issue: int, *, dry_run: bool = False, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
+          max_age_min: int = DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MIN,
+          now: datetime | None = None) -> list[str]:
+    """Answer every unanswered, recent ``ACCOUNTS:`` comment; the report lines.
+
+    Two bounds, both necessary: `limit` caps how far back the scan goes, and
+    `max_age_min` caps how old a directive may be and still be acted on.  A
+    stale one is reported in the janitor's line and NOT replied to, so the
+    owner's "no reply means it was not applied" rule still holds and a repeat
+    comment is answered normally.
+    """
+    login, source = owner_login()
+    comments = gh_common.api(f"issues/{issue}/comments", paginate=True) or []
+    applied = set(applied_ids())
+    report: list[str] = []
+    for row in comments[-limit:]:
+        body = row.get("body") or ""
+        if MARKER in body:  # one of our own replies
+            continue
+        directives = accounts_file.parse_directives(body)
+        if not directives:
+            continue
+        comment_id = int(row.get("id") or 0)
+        if not comment_id or already_answered(comments, comment_id):
+            continue
+        if comment_id in applied:
+            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} was already "
+                          "applied but its reply did not post; not applying it again")
+            continue
+        age = comment_age_min(row, now)
+        if max_age_min > 0 and age is not None and age > max_age_min:
+            report.append(
+                f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} is {age:.0f} min old "
+                f"(bound {max_age_min} min); NOT applied and not answered — capacity "
+                "advice this old is worse than none. Repeat it to apply it.")
+            continue
+        author = str((row.get("user") or {}).get("login") or "")
+        if author != login:
+            # Reported, never replied to.  A public reply echoing a stranger's
+            # text back let anyone with comment access make the bot comment once
+            # per comment they wrote.  The author check is the load-bearing part
+            # and is unchanged; the attempt is still visible, in the janitor's
+            # own report, where the owner reads it.
+            report += [
+                f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} by "
+                f"@{sanitize(author, 40) or 'an unknown account'}: ignored — this "
+                f"channel applies only the repository owner's comments ({login}, "
+                f"from {source}); {record['raw']}"
+                for record in directives]
+            continue
+        if dry_run:
+            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: comment {comment_id} by @{author}: "
+                          f"{len(directives)} directive(s) would be applied (dry run)")
+            continue
+        record_applied(comment_id)
+        results = accounts_file.apply_directives(
+            body, actor=f"github:{author}", origin=f"#{issue} comment {comment_id}")
+        gh_common.ensure_pr_comment(issue, reply_marker(comment_id),
+                                    render_reply(comment_id, author, results))
+        for line in results:
+            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} "
+                          f"by @{author}: {line}")
+    if not report:
+        report.append("accounts-inbox: no new ACCOUNTS: directive")
+    return report
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        prog="accounts_inbox.py", description=__doc__.splitlines()[0],
+        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    parser.add_argument("--issue", type=int,
+                        help="owner inbox issue (default: run_mode.py get owner_inbox_issue)")
+    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=DEFAULT_LIMIT,
+                        help=f"newest comments to consider (default {DEFAULT_LIMIT})")
+    parser.add_argument("--max-age-min", type=int, default=DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MIN,
+                        help="ignore directives older than this many minutes "
+                             f"(default {DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MIN}; 0 disables the bound)")
+    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
+                        help="print what would be applied and replied; write nothing")
+    parser.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="report as JSON")
+    args = parser.parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
+    try:
+        issue = args.issue
+        if issue is None:
+            # Not strict about the accounts file: this channel is the owner's
+            # REMOTE repair path for that very file, and it must not be dead
+            # exactly when a mistyped field needs repairing from a phone.
+            issue = int(run_mode.value_for(
+                run_mode.load_mode(strict_accounts=False), "owner_inbox_issue"))
+        report = sweep(issue, dry_run=args.dry_run, limit=max(1, args.limit),
+                       max_age_min=max(0, args.max_age_min))
+    except (LayerError, accounts_file.AccountsError, ValueError, OSError) as exc:
+        sys.stderr.write(f"accounts_inbox.py: {exc}\n")
+        return 2
+    if args.json:
+        json.dump(report, sys.stdout, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
+        sys.stdout.write("\n")
+    else:
+        sys.stdout.write("\n".join(report) + "\n")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

--- a/local/bin/janitor.sh

@@ -1,199 +1,210 @@
 #!/usr/bin/env bash
 #
 # Usage: local/bin/janitor.sh [--dry-run] [--pass NAME]... [--list-passes]
 #                             [--no-lock] [--report PATH] [--help]
 #
 # The self-repair pass.  ONE idempotent sweep, safe to run from cron or from the
 # merge daemon's loop, that turns every terminal state the pipeline can reach
 # into either a repair or a reported line.  Everything it does is selected by a
 # record field — a session status, a marker's reason string, a PR state, a spool
 # deadline — and never by a date glob or a filename digit filter.  The
 # 2026-09-12 recovery script globbed `*20260912*.jsonl` and matched
 # `/[0-9]{3}\.needs-attention$` with `-mmin -15`, so lanes below 100 and the 1xxx
 # lanes were never repaired and a marker missed by one poll was never picked up
 # again.  Nothing here has an age filter or a digit-count filter.
 #
 # The five passes, each independently guarded (one failing pass never aborts the
 # others; a GitHub error is reported and retried next pass, never converted into
 # a local success):
 #
 #   dead-sessions   results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl rows whose last status is
 #                   `active` and whose process is gone.  When the capture ends in
 #                   an exhausted reconnect, a 5xx or a concurrency refusal the
 #                   same role is re-dispatched on the same PR and the same head,
 #                   at most twice per (pr, role, head_sha), ledger
 #                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/retries.jsonl.  A capture that
 #                   ends cleanly is NEVER re-dispatched.  The abandoned row is
 #                   marked `failed` so telemetry stops showing it live.
 #                   This is the recovery path for the 25 reviews that were re-run
 #                   by hand after the 503 outage: review.sh retries only a
 #                   pre-model death (ended-started < 15 s and tokens 0), so a
 #                   reviewer that dies after twenty minutes at
 #                   "Reconnecting... 5/5" leaves the PR pending forever.
 #                   SCOPE: only a role with a re-dispatch entry point is
 #                   re-dispatched, and today that is `reviewer` alone
 #                   (review.sh, exact head, verdict supersedes).  A dead prover,
 #                   orc or fixer is marked `failed` with a `residue` field in
 #                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/actions.jsonl and is the owning
 #                   session's to re-plan; `local/bin/ready_report.py` counts
 #                   those rows PER ROLE into the hourly comment on the progress
 #                   issue, so the unrepaired remainder reaches the owner's
 #                   channel instead of a local log.
 #   parked-lanes    every $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/lanes/*.needs-attention, no digit
 #                   filter and no age filter.  The recorded reason is classified;
 #                   `merge` and `build` go to fix-lane.sh with the committed
 #                   brief, at most twice per lane; every other class stays parked
 #                   and appears in the report.
 #   superseded-prs  local/bin/pr_janitor.py (empty three-dot diff AND head
 #                   reachable from github/main; one idempotent marker comment;
 #                   never closes an issue).
 #   stale-lanes     lane state for lanes whose PR is closed or merged is deleted
 #                   (20 stale 1xxx lanes were left behind on 2026-09-12).
 #   spool-expiry    $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/capacity/spool/*.json entries past the
 #                   run's dispatch_cutoff are dropped, so a spool that outlives a
 #                   run cannot re-launch stale work.
+#   owner-accounts  `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>]
+#                   [enabled=true|false]` comments on the owner inbox issue are
+#                   applied to the live accounts file and answered with one
+#                   `applied:` / `rejected:` reply per comment
+#                   (local/bin/accounts_inbox.py).  ONLY comments written by the
+#                   repository owner login are applied; the author check, the
+#                   parsing and the validation live in that tool and in
+#                   local/bin/accounts_file.py, never here.  It is the owner's
+#                   channel for a ceiling change when they are away from a
+#                   shell: on 2026-09-12 every such change was a message to a
+#                   session that had to be idle to receive it.
 #
 # The janitor repairs; it never merges, never pushes, never closes an issue and
 # never touches a gate.  Repairs are dispatched through fix-lane.sh ->
 # dispatch.sh (agents never invoke codex directly) and the lane tail is
 # relaunched through the repository's own local/bin/lane.sh.
 #
 # Runner: results/telemetry/owner-tools/merge-daemon.sh calls this once every
 # `janitor_interval_s` (daemon.conf), detached and bounded; the sweep takes its
 # own lock, so an overlapping call exits instead of doubling up.  Nothing else
 # runs it: a checkout whose merge daemon is not running has no self-repair.
 #
 # Output: one line per action on stdout, the same lines in
 # $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/report.md (the operator's log of the sweep; the
 # hourly readiness report does NOT read it — it reports merges and readiness
 # from daemon state) and one append-only JSONL row per action in
 # $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/{retries,repairs,actions,closures}.jsonl.
 #
 # Exit codes: 0 all passes completed; 1 at least one pass failed (the others
 # still ran); 2 usage/environment error.
 #
 # Environment:
 #   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT             override ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev
 #   MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT              override the checkout (default: this file's)
 #   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_RETRY_CAP      re-dispatches per (pr, role, head)  [2]
 #   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPAIR_CAP     repairs per lane                    [2]
 #   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_STALE_S        a dead session's capture must be this old
 #                                    before it is judged abandoned       [900]
 #   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_LANE_KEEP_S    lane state younger than this is never
 #                                    deleted                             [3600]
 #   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES  roles the janitor may re-dispatch
 #                                    automatically; only a role with an entry
 #                                    point below may be listed    [reviewer]
 #   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_CLASSIFIER     auto | builtin  (auto prefers telemetry.py's
 #                                    classify-failure when it exists)    [auto]
 #   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_SOURCE_ONLY=1  define the functions and return; run nothing
 #                                    (used by scripts/tests/test_janitor_classify.py)
 
 set -uo pipefail
 
 PROG="janitor.sh"
 
 SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
 REPO_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT:-$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)}"
 CACHE_ROOT="${MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT:-$HOME/.cache/mipstarre-dev}"
 W="$CACHE_ROOT/watchdog"
 L="$W/lanes"
 D="$W/daemon"
 J="$W/janitor"
 SPOOL="$W/capacity/spool"
 SESSIONS="${MIPSTARRE_SESSIONS_JSONL:-$REPO_ROOT/results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl}"
 
 RETRY_CAP="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_RETRY_CAP:-2}"
 REPAIR_CAP="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPAIR_CAP:-2}"
 STALE_S="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_STALE_S:-900}"
 LANE_KEEP_S="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_LANE_KEEP_S:-3600}"
 REDISPATCH_ROLES="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES:-reviewer}"
 CLASSIFIER="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_CLASSIFIER:-auto}"
 BASE_REF="${MIPSTARRE_BASE_REF:-github/main}"
 
 DRY_RUN=0
 USE_LOCK=1
 REPORT_FILE=""
 PASS_FAILURES=0
 
-ALL_PASSES="dead-sessions parked-lanes superseded-prs stale-lanes spool-expiry"
+ALL_PASSES="dead-sessions parked-lanes superseded-prs stale-lanes spool-expiry owner-accounts"
 SELECTED="$ALL_PASSES"
 
 # Report lines are collected in a file, not a variable: each pass runs in its own
 # subshell so that one failing pass cannot abort the others, and a variable would
 # not survive that boundary.
 REPORT_SPOOL="${MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPORT_SPOOL:-$J/.report-lines.$$}"
 
 # --------------------------------------------------------------- small helpers
 
 now() { date -u +%FT%TZ; }
 
 log() { printf '== %s %s\n' "$(now)" "$*"; }
 
 # A reported line: printed, kept for report.md, and never silent.
 report() {
   printf '%s\n' "$*"
   mkdir -p "$(dirname "$REPORT_SPOOL")" 2>/dev/null || return 0
   printf '%s\n' "$*" >> "$REPORT_SPOOL" 2>/dev/null || true

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""The owner-inbox comment channel for the live accounts file.
+
+`local/bin/accounts_inbox.py` applies `ACCOUNTS:` comments on the owner inbox
+issue and answers each one.  Three properties are load-bearing and are what
+these cases check: only the repository owner's comments are applied, a comment
+is applied exactly once however often the janitor sweeps, and every directive —
+applied or rejected — is echoed back so the owner knows what took effect.
+
+`gh` is never invoked: `gh_common.api` is replaced by a fake GitHub that serves
+a comment list and records the writes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import contextlib
+import io
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "local" / "bin"))
+
+import accounts_file as af  # noqa: E402
+import accounts_inbox as inbox  # noqa: E402
+
+OWNER = "Dengnifer"
+ISSUE = 500
+
+BRIEF_ROWS = [
+    {"name": "primary", "label": "relay-us7", "endpoint": "relay-us7",
+     "codex_home": "~/.codex", "nominal_limit": 5, "external_reserved": 0,
+     "enabled": True},
+    {"name": "second", "label": "space", "endpoint": "api.finite-dimensional.space",
+     "codex_home": "~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/codex-home-yxy", "nominal_limit": 30,
+     "external_reserved": 2, "enabled": True},
+]
+
+
+class FakeGitHub:
+    """Just enough of the REST surface: list comments, create one, patch one."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.comments: list[dict] = []
+        self.posted: list[dict] = []
+        self.next_id = 1000
+
+    def comment(self, body: str, login: str) -> int:
+        self.next_id += 1
+        self.comments.append({"id": self.next_id, "body": body,
+                              "user": {"login": login}})
+        return self.next_id
+
+    def api(self, path, *, method=None, payload=None, paginate=False,
+            mutation=False, idempotent=False, absolute=False):
+        if path.startswith(f"issues/{ISSUE}/comments") and method is None:
+            return list(self.comments)
+        if path.startswith(f"issues/{ISSUE}/comments") and method == "POST":
+            number = self.comment(payload["body"], "github-actions")
+            self.posted.append(payload)
+            return {"id": number}
+        if path.startswith("issues/comments/") and method == "PATCH":
+            self.posted.append(payload)
+            return {"id": 0}
+        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected API call {method or 'GET'} {path}")
+
+
+class InboxHarness(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self.tmp.cleanup)
+        self.cache = Path(self.tmp.name) / "cache"
+        (self.cache / "watchdog").mkdir(parents=True)
+        environment = mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {
+            "MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT": str(self.cache),
+            "MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN": OWNER,
+        })
+        environment.start()
+        self.addCleanup(environment.stop)
+        af.seed(BRIEF_ROWS, root=self.cache, source="test")
+        self.github = FakeGitHub()
+        patched = mock.patch.object(inbox.gh_common, "api", self.github.api)
+        patched.start()
+        self.addCleanup(patched.stop)
+
+    def sweep(self, **kwargs) -> list[str]:
+        out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
+        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
+            report = inbox.sweep(ISSUE, **kwargs)
+        return report
+
+    def ceiling(self, name: str) -> int:
+        return af.load_map(self.cache)[name]["ceiling"]
+
+
+class TestOwnerChannel(InboxHarness):
+    def test_an_owner_directive_is_applied_and_answered(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("The admin took slots back.\n"
+                            "ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", OWNER)
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 20)
+        self.assertTrue(any("applied: second" in line for line in report))
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.posted), 1)
+        body = self.github.posted[0]["body"]
+        self.assertIn("applied: second ceiling 30 -> 20", body)
+        self.assertIn(inbox.MARKER, body)
+
+    def test_several_directives_in_one_comment(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=12 reserved=4\n"
+                            "ACCOUNTS: primary enabled=false\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        entries = af.load_map(self.cache)
+        self.assertEqual(entries["second"]["ceiling"], 12)
+        self.assertEqual(entries["second"]["external_reserved"], 4)
+        self.assertFalse(entries["primary"]["enabled"])
+
+    def test_a_comment_by_anyone_else_is_ignored_and_reported(self) -> None:
+        # Never applied, and never answered in public: replying echoed the
+        # stranger's own text back, so anyone with comment access could make the
+        # bot comment once per comment they wrote.  The attempt stays visible —
+        # in the janitor's report, which is where the owner reads it.
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=999\n", "a-stranger")
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 30)
+        self.assertTrue(any("a-stranger" in line for line in report))
+        self.assertTrue(any("repository owner" in line for line in report))
+        self.assertEqual(self.github.posted, [])
+
+    def test_a_comment_is_applied_exactly_once(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        # The owner then lowers it further at the shell; a second sweep must not
+        # re-apply the comment and undo that.
+        entries = af.load(self.cache)
+        af.apply_fields(entries, "second", {"ceiling": "8"})
+        af.save(entries, root=self.cache, actor="owner", action="set", detail="8")
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 8)
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.posted), 1)
+        self.assertIn("no new ACCOUNTS: directive", report[0])
+
+    def test_prose_without_a_directive_is_left_alone(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("Can you raise the yxy key a bit?", OWNER)
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.github.posted, [])
+        self.assertIn("no new ACCOUNTS: directive", report[0])
+
+    def test_a_bad_directive_is_answered_with_the_reason(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: fourth ceiling=3\n"
+                            "ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=notanumber\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 30)
+        body = self.github.posted[0]["body"]
+        self.assertIn("no account named 'fourth'", body)
+        self.assertIn("nonnegative whole number", body)
+
+    def test_dry_run_writes_nothing(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", OWNER)
+        report = self.sweep(dry_run=True)
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 30)
+        self.assertEqual(self.github.posted, [])
+        self.assertTrue(any("dry run" in line for line in report))
+
+    def test_our_own_reply_is_never_read_as_a_directive(self) -> None:
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        # The reply quotes the rejected directive lines verbatim; re-reading it
+        # as input would loop the channel against itself.
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: nope ceiling=1\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertIn("no new ACCOUNTS: directive", report[0])
+
+
+class TestStaleness(InboxHarness):
+    """A directive the janitor never saw is stale capacity advice.
+
+    The count cap alone did not implement the module's own rule: the owner inbox
+    issue is permissions-only and low traffic, so every `ACCOUNTS:` comment ever
+    written stayed in scope forever.  With the pipeline deliberately paused, the
+    first sweep after a resume would have applied the whole backlog at once —
+    `enabled=false` included, which is cap 0 and no probe.
+    """
+
+    def old_comment(self, body: str, minutes: int) -> int:
+        number = self.github.comment(body, OWNER)
+        moment = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=minutes)
+        self.github.comments[-1]["created_at"] = \
+            moment.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
+        return number
+
+    def test_a_day_old_directive_is_neither_applied_nor_answered(self) -> None:
+        self.old_comment("ACCOUNTS: second enabled=false\n", 60 * 24)
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 30)
+        self.assertTrue(af.load_map(self.cache)["second"]["enabled"])
+        self.assertEqual(self.github.posted, [])
+        self.assertTrue(any("NOT applied" in line for line in report))
+
+    def test_a_recent_directive_still_applies(self) -> None:
+        self.old_comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", 5)
+        self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 20)
+        self.assertEqual(len(self.github.posted), 1)
+
+    def test_a_comment_with_no_timestamp_is_not_treated_as_stale(self) -> None:
+        # The REST API always supplies created_at; a missing one is an unusual
+        # payload, not an old comment, and dropping it would lose a real edit.
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=18\n", OWNER)
+        self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 18)
+
+    def test_the_bound_can_be_turned_off(self) -> None:
+        self.old_comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", 60 * 24)
+        self.sweep(max_age_min=0)
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 20)
+
+
+class TestApplyOnce(InboxHarness):
+    def test_a_failed_reply_does_not_re_apply_the_directive(self) -> None:
+        # apply_directives writes the file; the reply marker lives on GitHub and
+        # is written after it.  If that POST fails, the next sweep must not
+        # re-apply the same directive and revert an `accounts.sh set` the owner
+        # made in between.
+        self.github.comment("ACCOUNTS: second ceiling=20\n", OWNER)
+        with mock.patch.object(inbox.gh_common, "ensure_pr_comment",
+                               side_effect=OSError("rate limited")):
+            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
+                self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 20)
+        af.apply_fields(entries := af.load(self.cache), "second", {"ceiling": "9"})
+        af.save(entries, root=self.cache, actor="owner", action="set", detail="shell")
+        report = self.sweep()
+        self.assertEqual(self.ceiling("second"), 9)
+        self.assertTrue(any("already applied" in line for line in report))
+
+
+class TestOwnerLogin(InboxHarness):
+    def test_the_environment_wins(self) -> None:
+        login, source = inbox.owner_login()
+        self.assertEqual(login, OWNER)
+        self.assertIn("MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN", source)
+
+    def test_the_readme_line_is_the_recorded_source(self) -> None:
+        with mock.patch.dict(os.environ, {"MIPSTARRE_OWNER_LOGIN": ""}):
+            login, source = inbox.owner_login(REPO_ROOT)
+        self.assertEqual(login, OWNER)
+        self.assertIn("README.md", source)
+
+    def test_local_readme_actually_carries_the_line(self) -> None:
+        # The parser reads exactly one documented line; if the README is
+        # reworded without it, the channel silently falls back to the repository
+        # slug, so the line is part of the contract and is checked here.
+        text = (REPO_ROOT / "local" / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+        self.assertRegex(text, inbox.OWNER_LINE_RE)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	#
     3	# Usage: local/bin/janitor.sh [--dry-run] [--pass NAME]... [--list-passes]
     4	#                             [--no-lock] [--report PATH] [--help]
     5	#
     6	# The self-repair pass.  ONE idempotent sweep, safe to run from cron or from the
     7	# merge daemon's loop, that turns every terminal state the pipeline can reach
     8	# into either a repair or a reported line.  Everything it does is selected by a
     9	# record field — a session status, a marker's reason string, a PR state, a spool
    10	# deadline — and never by a date glob or a filename digit filter.  The
    11	# 2026-09-12 recovery script globbed `*20260912*.jsonl` and matched
    12	# `/[0-9]{3}\.needs-attention$` with `-mmin -15`, so lanes below 100 and the 1xxx
    13	# lanes were never repaired and a marker missed by one poll was never picked up
    14	# again.  Nothing here has an age filter or a digit-count filter.
    15	#
    16	# The five passes, each independently guarded (one failing pass never aborts the
    17	# others; a GitHub error is reported and retried next pass, never converted into
    18	# a local success):
    19	#
    20	#   dead-sessions   results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl rows whose last status is
    21	#                   `active` and whose process is gone.  When the capture ends in
    22	#                   an exhausted reconnect, a 5xx or a concurrency refusal the
    23	#                   same role is re-dispatched on the same PR and the same head,
    24	#                   at most twice per (pr, role, head_sha), ledger
    25	#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/retries.jsonl.  A capture that
    26	#                   ends cleanly is NEVER re-dispatched.  The abandoned row is
    27	#                   marked `failed` so telemetry stops showing it live.
    28	#                   This is the recovery path for the 25 reviews that were re-run
    29	#                   by hand after the 503 outage: review.sh retries only a
    30	#                   pre-model death (ended-started < 15 s and tokens 0), so a
    31	#                   reviewer that dies after twenty minutes at
    32	#                   "Reconnecting... 5/5" leaves the PR pending forever.
    33	#                   SCOPE: only a role with a re-dispatch entry point is
    34	#                   re-dispatched, and today that is `reviewer` alone
    35	#                   (review.sh, exact head, verdict supersedes).  A dead prover,
    36	#                   orc or fixer is marked `failed` with a `residue` field in
    37	#                   $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/actions.jsonl and is the owning
    38	#                   session's to re-plan; `local/bin/ready_report.py` counts
    39	#                   those rows PER ROLE into the hourly comment on the progress
    40	#                   issue, so the unrepaired remainder reaches the owner's
    41	#                   channel instead of a local log.
    42	#   parked-lanes    every $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/lanes/*.needs-attention, no digit
    43	#                   filter and no age filter.  The recorded reason is classified;
    44	#                   `merge` and `build` go to fix-lane.sh with the committed
    45	#                   brief, at most twice per lane; every other class stays parked
    46	#                   and appears in the report.
    47	#   superseded-prs  local/bin/pr_janitor.py (empty three-dot diff AND head
    48	#                   reachable from github/main; one idempotent marker comment;
    49	#                   never closes an issue).
    50	#   stale-lanes     lane state for lanes whose PR is closed or merged is deleted
    51	#                   (20 stale 1xxx lanes were left behind on 2026-09-12).
    52	#   spool-expiry    $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/capacity/spool/*.json entries past the
    53	#                   run's dispatch_cutoff are dropped, so a spool that outlives a
    54	#                   run cannot re-launch stale work.
    55	#   owner-accounts  `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>]
    56	#                   [enabled=true|false]` comments on the owner inbox issue are
    57	#                   applied to the live accounts file and answered with one
    58	#                   `applied:` / `rejected:` reply per comment
    59	#                   (local/bin/accounts_inbox.py).  ONLY comments written by the
    60	#                   repository owner login are applied; the author check, the
    61	#                   parsing and the validation live in that tool and in
    62	#                   local/bin/accounts_file.py, never here.  It is the owner's
    63	#                   channel for a ceiling change when they are away from a
    64	#                   shell: on 2026-09-12 every such change was a message to a
    65	#                   session that had to be idle to receive it.
    66	#
    67	# The janitor repairs; it never merges, never pushes, never closes an issue and
    68	# never touches a gate.  Repairs are dispatched through fix-lane.sh ->
    69	# dispatch.sh (agents never invoke codex directly) and the lane tail is
    70	# relaunched through the repository's own local/bin/lane.sh.
    71	#
    72	# Runner: results/telemetry/owner-tools/merge-daemon.sh calls this once every
    73	# `janitor_interval_s` (daemon.conf), detached and bounded; the sweep takes its
    74	# own lock, so an overlapping call exits instead of doubling up.  Nothing else
    75	# runs it: a checkout whose merge daemon is not running has no self-repair.
    76	#
    77	# Output: one line per action on stdout, the same lines in
    78	# $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/report.md (the operator's log of the sweep; the
    79	# hourly readiness report does NOT read it — it reports merges and readiness
    80	# from daemon state) and one append-only JSONL row per action in
    81	# $CACHE_ROOT/watchdog/janitor/{retries,repairs,actions,closures}.jsonl.
    82	#
    83	# Exit codes: 0 all passes completed; 1 at least one pass failed (the others
    84	# still ran); 2 usage/environment error.
    85	#
    86	# Environment:
    87	#   MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT             override ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev
    88	#   MIPSTARRE_REPO_ROOT              override the checkout (default: this file's)
    89	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_RETRY_CAP      re-dispatches per (pr, role, head)  [2]
    90	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REPAIR_CAP     repairs per lane                    [2]
    91	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_STALE_S        a dead session's capture must be this old
    92	#                                    before it is judged abandoned       [900]
    93	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_LANE_KEEP_S    lane state younger than this is never
    94	#                                    deleted                             [3600]
    95	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_REDISPATCH_ROLES  roles the janitor may re-dispatch
    96	#                                    automatically; only a role with an entry
    97	#                                    point below may be listed    [reviewer]
    98	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_CLASSIFIER     auto | builtin  (auto prefers telemetry.py's
    99	#                                    classify-failure when it exists)    [auto]
   100	#   MIPSTARRE_JANITOR_SOURCE_ONLY=1  define the functions and return; run nothing
   101	#                                    (used by scripts/tests/test_janitor_classify.py)

   144	# A reported line: printed, kept for report.md, and never silent.

   155	# Append-only JSONL under the cache root.  One short line per append, written
   156	# with a single write(2), which is atomic for a line this size; the janitor also

   164	# Count attempt rows in a ledger for one key.  Field-based, never a date glob.
   165	ledger_count() {
   166	  JAN_LEDGER="$1" JAN_KEY="$2" python3 - <<'PY'
   167	import json, os
   168	path, key, total = os.environ["JAN_LEDGER"], os.environ["JAN_KEY"], 0
   169	try:
   170	    with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as handle:
   171	        for line in handle:
   172	            line = line.strip()
   173	            if not line:
   174	                continue
   175	            try:
   176	                row = json.loads(line)
   177	            except ValueError:
   178	                continue
   179	            if isinstance(row, dict) and row.get("key") == key and row.get("event") == "attempt":
   180	                total += 1
   760	      account "$account" worktree "$worktree" capture_class "$class" reason "$reason"
   761	    ( cd "$REPO_ROOT" && MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT="$CACHE_ROOT" \
   762	        $DETACH nohup "$cmd" "$pr" > "$log_file" 2>&1 < /dev/null & )
   763	    report "janitor: dead session $name (PR $pr, $role, head ${head:0:12}) ended '$class' -> re-dispatched, log $log_file"

   765	      session "$name" role "$role" pr "$pr" head "$head" capture_class "$class" log "$log_file"

   767	$rows
   768	EOF

   774	pass_parked_lanes() {
   775	  local marker lane text class branch pr fixer mode seen
   776	  local found=0
   777	  while IFS= read -r marker; do
   778	    [ -n "$marker" ] || continue
   779	    found=1
   780	    if ! lane="$(lane_id_of "$marker")"; then
   781	      report "janitor: parked lane: $marker has no lane number -> reported, untouched"
   782	      continue
   783	    fi
   784	    text="$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$marker" 2>/dev/null)"
   785	    class="$(classify_reason "$text")"
   786	    branch="$(lane_branch "$lane")"
   787	    if ! repairable_class "$class"; then
   788	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class${branch:+, branch $branch}) -> stays parked: ${text:0:120}"
   789	      continue
   790	    fi
   791	    if lane_is_running "$lane"; then
   792	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class) but a lane process is running -> left alone"
   793	      continue
   794	    fi
   795	    if [ -z "$branch" ]; then
   796	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class) but its branch could not be resolved from the record -> stays parked"
   797	      continue
   798	    fi
   799	    pr="$(pr_for_branch "$branch")"
   800	    if [ -z "$pr" ]; then
   801	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class, branch $branch) has no open PR -> stays parked (see the stale-lanes pass)"
   802	      continue
   803	    fi
   804	    if fixer_is_running "$pr"; then
   805	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class, PR $pr): a repair is already running -> left alone"
   806	      continue
   807	    fi
   808	    if ! repair_allow "$lane"; then
   809	      seen="$(ledger_count "$J/repairs.jsonl" "lane:$lane")"
   810	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class, PR $pr): repair cap reached ($seen/$REPAIR_CAP) -> stays parked for the operator"
   811	      continue
   812	    fi
   813	    if ! fixer="$(fix_lane_cmd)"; then
   814	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class, PR $pr): no fix-lane.sh installed or in the checkout -> stays parked"
   815	      continue
   816	    fi
   817	    mode="$class"
   818	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
   819	      report "janitor: lane $lane parked (class $class, PR $pr, branch $branch): would run $fixer $pr $lane $branch $mode (dry run)"
   820	      continue
   821	    fi

   823	    # leaves an empty file that daemon-scan.py's load_marker degrades to class
   824	    # `infra`, whose five-minute backoff clears it — so the "hold this PR while
   825	    # it is repaired" marker would last five minutes and the daemon would queue
   826	    # the PR back into the repair that is still running.
   827	    write_repair_marker "$pr" "$lane" "$class" "$text"
   828	    ledger_append "$J/actions.jsonl" ts "$(now)" pass parked-lanes action repair lane "$lane" \
   829	      pr "$pr" branch "$branch" class "$class" tool "$fixer"
   830	    ( cd "$REPO_ROOT" \

   832	         $DETACH nohup bash "$fixer" "$pr" "$lane" "$branch" "$mode" \

   861	pass_stale_lanes() {
   862	  local lane branch state pr_state pr_number file newest
   863	  local seen="" removed=0 examined=0
   864	  [ -d "$L" ] || { report "janitor: stale-lanes: no lane state"; return 0; }
   865	  for file in "$L"/*; do
   866	    [ -e "$file" ] || continue
   867	    lane="$(lane_id_of "$file")" || continue

   874	    # Freshness is the age of the YOUNGEST file of the lane: state a lane still
   875	    # writes is never deleted, whatever the PR says.
   876	    newest="$(python3 - "$L" "$lane" <<'PY'
   877	import os, sys, time
   878	directory, lane = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   879	ages = []
   880	for name in os.listdir(directory):
   881	    if name.split(".")[0] == lane:
   882	        try:
   883	            ages.append(time.time() - os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(directory, name)))
   884	        except OSError:
   885	            pass
   886	print(int(min(ages)) if ages else 0)
   887	PY
   888	)"
   889	    if [ "${newest:-0}" -lt "$LANE_KEEP_S" ]; then
   890	      continue
   891	    fi

   895	      continue
   896	    fi

   900	    if [ -z "$pr_state" ] || [ -z "$pr_number" ]; then
   901	      report "janitor: lane $lane ($branch): no PR found for the branch -> lane state kept, reported"
   902	      continue
   903	    fi

   905	      closed|merged) ;;
   906	      *) continue ;;
   907	    esac
   908	    if [ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]; then
   909	      report "janitor: lane $lane ($branch): PR $pr_number is $state -> would delete $(ls "$L/$lane".* 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ') lane state file(s) (dry run)"
   910	      continue
   911	    fi
   912	    ledger_append "$J/actions.jsonl" ts "$(now)" pass stale-lanes action delete-lane-state \
   913	      lane "$lane" branch "$branch" pr "$pr_number" pr_state "$state" \
   914	      files "$(ls "$L/$lane".* 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
   915	    rm -f "$L/$lane".*
   916	    removed=$((removed + 1))

   918	  done
   919	  report "janitor: stale-lanes: $examined lane(s) examined, $removed cleared (state younger than ${LANE_KEEP_S}s is never touched)"

   429	def observe(rows: list[dict], name: str, endpoints: dict[str, str], roles: dict[str, str],
   430	            now: datetime, *, counter_window_s: int, fivexx_window_s: int,
   431	            disabling: tuple[str, ...] = ()) -> dict:
   432	    """Refusal, death and key-invalidating counters for one account.
   433	
   434	    A ``failure_class`` the policy does not name — including the literal
   435	    ``unknown`` — is counted in neither direction, so a reworded provider message
   436	    leaves the cap where a hand-set cap would have been instead of collapsing it.
   437	
   438	    ``disabling`` names the classes that say the KEY is unusable rather than busy
   439	    (``auth``, ``insufficient_balance``).  They are collected separately, with
   440	    their detail, because the answer to them is "disable this key and say why",
   441	    not "lower the cap by a quarter".
   442	    """
   443	    bucket: dict[str, Any] = {"refusals": 0, "deaths": 0, "neutral": 0,
   444	                              "deaths_by_class": {}, "refusal_times": [], "fivexx_times": [],
   445	                              "disable_times": [], "disable_class": "", "disable_detail": ""}
   446	    counter_since = now - timedelta(seconds=counter_window_s)
   447	    fivexx_since = now - timedelta(seconds=fivexx_window_s)
   448	    for row in rows:
   449	        # ``account`` FIRST.  The dispatcher writes the name it actually routed
   450	        # to; an endpoint is shared by up to two keys in the owner's own topology
   451	        # (one to three endpoints, one or two keys each).  Matching the endpoint
   452	        # first attributed a refusal to whichever key happened to be written into
   453	        # the endpoint map last, so AIMD cut the innocent key while the refusing
   454	        # one crept up, and one `auth` row disabled the wrong key at threshold 1.
   455	        owner = next((endpoints[row[field]] for field in
   456	                      ("account", "endpoint", "failure_endpoint", "key_label")
   457	                      if isinstance(row.get(field), str) and row[field] in endpoints), None)
   458	        failure_class = row.get("failure_class")
   459	        if owner != name or not isinstance(failure_class, str) or not failure_class:
   460	            continue
   461	        if failure_class == "endpoint_5xx" and row["_ts"] >= fivexx_since:
   462	            bucket["fivexx_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   463	        if row["_ts"] < counter_since:
   464	            continue
   465	        if failure_class in disabling:
   466	            bucket["disable_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   467	            bucket["disable_class"] = failure_class
   468	            bucket["disable_detail"] = str(row.get("failure_detail") or "")[:120]
   469	        role = roles.get(failure_class, "neutral")
   470	        if role == "refusal":
   471	            bucket["refusals"] += 1
   472	            bucket["refusal_times"].append(row["_ts"])
   473	        elif role == "death":
   474	            bucket["deaths"] += 1
   475	            bucket["deaths_by_class"][failure_class] = \
   476	                bucket["deaths_by_class"].get(failure_class, 0) + 1
   477	        else:
   478	            bucket["neutral"] += 1
   479	    bucket["refusal_times"].sort()
   480	    bucket["fivexx_times"].sort()
   481	    bucket["disable_times"].sort()
   482	    return bucket

   547	def write_cap_files(caps: dict[str, int]) -> int:
   548	    """Write the legacy derived outputs; ``max-codex`` is mechanically the sum.
   549	
   550	    It therefore cannot disagree with the per-account files.  It is a display and
   551	    lane-parallelism value only: admission reads the per-account files
   552	    (``local/protocols/capacity.md`` §4).
   553	    """
   554	    effective = {name: int(value) for name, value in caps.items()}
   555	    directory = watchdog_dir()
   556	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   557	    # A cap file for an account that has dropped out of the configured set is
   558	    # ZEROED, not deleted.  Deleting it would break the "never an empty read"
   559	    # property; leaving its old number is worse still, because that stale file is
   560	    # exactly what `account_router.account_names()` picks up from its
   561	    # ``max-codex-*`` glob when accounts.json is unreadable — a key the owner
   562	    # removed would go on being admitted at the ceiling it had when they removed
   563	    # it.  The two historical names keep a file unconditionally, so a reader that
   564	    # predates this layer still finds a number.
   565	    stale = sorted(path.name[len("max-codex-"):] for path in
   566	                   directory.glob("max-codex-*")
   567	                   if path.is_file() and path.name != "max-codex"
   568	                   and path.name[len("max-codex-"):] not in effective)
   569	    for name in (*DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS, *stale,
   570	                 *(name for name in effective if name not in DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS)):
   571	        _write_cap_file(directory / f"max-codex-{name}", effective.get(name, 0))
   572	    _write_cap_file(directory / "max-codex", sum(effective.values()))
   573	    return sum(effective.values())

   579	def probe_account(account: str, codex_home: str, timeout_s: int) -> bool:

   581	
   582	    A health check, not a work session: read-only sandbox, no persona, no task,

   602	def _try_probe(account: str, codex_home: str, timeout_s: int) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
   603	    """``(ran, succeeded)`` — single-flight, so two ticks cannot probe at once."""
   604	    capacity_dir().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   605	    with (capacity_dir() / f"probe-{account}.lock").open("a") as lock:
   606	        try:
   607	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   608	        except OSError:
   609	            return False, False
   610	        try:
   611	            return True, probe_account(account, codex_home, timeout_s)
   612	        finally:
   613	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

   616	def update_health(account: str, health: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, now: datetime,
   617	                  *, no_probe: bool, codex_home: str, probe_timeout_s: int) -> str:
   618	    """Advance the endpoint health machine one tick; returns what it did.
   619	
   620	    Independent of AIMD in both directions: a refusal never changes health and a
   621	    5xx never runs the AIMD arithmetic.
   622	
   623	    Two kinds of trip, one machine.  ``endpoint_5xx`` says the ENDPOINT is down
   624	    and needs ``fivexx_threshold`` deaths inside ``fivexx_window_s`` — a single
   625	    502 is noise.  ``auth`` and ``insufficient_balance`` say the KEY is unusable
   626	    and trip at ``disable_threshold`` (1): a `401` is not a statistic, and
   627	    retrying an invalid key at any concurrency produces nothing but dead
   628	    sessions.  Both write the REASON into the health file, because "cap 0" with
   629	    no reason is the state the owner had to diagnose by reading captures on
   630	    2026-09-12; the way back is the same half-open probe, with the key-invalid
   631	    backoff starting longer (``disable_backoff_s``) since a key does not become
   632	    valid again in thirty seconds.
   633	    """
   634	    fivexx = len(counters["fivexx_times"])
   635	    disabling = len(counters.get("disable_times") or ())
   636	    base = knobs["probe_backoff_s"]
   637	    disable_base = max(base, int(knobs.get("disable_backoff_s",
   638	                                           _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_backoff_s"])))
   639	    health.update(consecutive_5xx=fivexx, key_failures=disabling, updated=ts(now))
   640	    if health["state"] != "down":
   641	        if disabling >= int(knobs.get("disable_threshold",
   642	                                      _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_threshold"])):
   643	            detail = counters.get("disable_detail") or ""
   644	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0,
   645	                          backoff_s=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]),
   646	                          reason=f"{counters.get('disable_class') or 'key'}: "
   647	                                 f"{detail or 'the key was refused'}",
   648	                          disabled_by=counters.get("disable_class") or "key",
   649	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(
   650	                              seconds=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]))))
   651	            return "trip"
   652	        if fivexx >= knobs["fivexx_threshold"]:
   653	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0, backoff_s=base,
   654	                          reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} deaths in "
   655	                                 f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s",
   656	                          disabled_by="endpoint_5xx",
   657	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(seconds=base)))
   658	            return "trip"
   659	        if fivexx:
   660	            if health["state"] != "degraded":
   661	                health.update(state="degraded", since=ts(now),
   662	                              reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} death(s) in "
   663	                                     f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s, below the "
   664	                                     f"threshold of {knobs['fivexx_threshold']}")
   665	            return "degraded"
   666	        if health["state"] != "up":
   667	            health.update(state="up", since=ts(now), reason="")
   668	            return "clear"
   669	        return "none"
   670	    if no_probe:  # an operator hold, or a key the brief disabled
   671	        return "probe-held"
   672	    due = parse_ts(health.get("next_probe_at"))
   673	    if due is not None and now < due:
   674	        return "probe-waiting"
   675	    ran, ok = _try_probe(account, codex_home, probe_timeout_s)
   676	    if not ran:
   677	        return "probe-inflight"
   678	    if not ok:
   679	        health["probes_ok"] = 0
   680	        health["backoff_s"] = min(int(health["backoff_s"]) * 2, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"])
   681	        health["next_probe_at"] = ts(now + timedelta(seconds=health["backoff_s"]))
   682	        return "probe-failed"
   683	    health["probes_ok"] = int(health["probes_ok"]) + 1
   684	    if health["probes_ok"] < knobs["probes_to_recover"]:
   685	        health["next_probe_at"] = ts(now + timedelta(seconds=base))
   686	        return "probe-ok"
   687	    health.update(state="up", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0, consecutive_5xx=0,
   688	                  key_failures=0, reason="", disabled_by="",
   689	                  backoff_s=base, next_probe_at=None)
   690	    return "recovered"

   795	def tick(now: datetime, *, policy: dict, run_mode: dict, state: dict,
   796	         dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
   797	    """One control step: health, then decrease, then increase, then the clamp."""
   798	    windows, roles = policy["windows"], class_roles(policy)
   799	    disabling = disabling_classes(policy)
   800	    hold = (capacity_dir() / "hold").exists()
   801	    paused = state.get("paused_at") is not None

   804	    lookback = max([windows["counter_window_s"]]
   805	                   + [health_knobs(policy, name)["fivexx_window_s"] for name in accounts])
   806	    rows = read_session_rows(telemetry_dir() / "sessions.jsonl",
   807	                             now - timedelta(seconds=lookback))
   808	    live, waiters = count_live(accounts), count_waiters()

   810	                               "waiters": waiters, "accounts": {}}

   813	        # that carry only that token are attributed to neither key.

   822	        counters = observe(rows, name, endpoints, roles, now,
   823	                           counter_window_s=windows["counter_window_s"],
   824	                           fivexx_window_s=hknobs["fivexx_window_s"],
   825	                           disabling=disabling)

   827	        floor, ceiling = refresh(account_state, entry, knobs)

   831	        # and the disabled account in suppressing the probe, so a pause can never
   832	        # fire `codex exec` on the owner's keys after the deadline.
   833	        action = update_health(name, health, counters, hknobs, now,
   834	                               no_probe=hold or paused or not entry["enabled"],
   835	                               codex_home=entry["codex_home"],
   836	                               probe_timeout_s=windows["probe_timeout_s"])
   837	        account_state["health"] = health["state"]
   838	        notes: list[str] = []
   839	        if hold:
   840	            notes.append("hold: cap frozen")
   841	        elif paused or not entry["enabled"]:
   842	            # BEFORE the recovery branch: a recovering endpoint must not raise
   843	            # the cap to 1 while state.json says paused (or while the brief says
   844	            # this key is off).  Pause outranks health in both directions.
   845	            if int(account_state["cap"]) != 0:  # a note per tick would be noise
   846	                notes.append("paused: cap 0" if paused
   847	                             else "disabled in the accounts file: cap 0, no probe")
   848	            account_state.update(cap=0, quiet_since=None, decrease_window_until=None)
   849	        elif action == "trip":
   850	            account_state.update(cap=0, quiet_since=None, decrease_window_until=None)
   851	            notes.append("endpoint down: cap 0")
   852	        elif action == "recovered":
   853	            # Never back to the pre-outage cap: the endpoint that just came back
   854	            # is the last thing to hand twenty sessions.
   855	            account_state.update(cap=clamp(1, floor, ceiling), quiet_since=None,
   856	                                 decrease_window_until=None, refusal_cursor=None)

   858	        elif health["state"] == "down":
   859	            account_state["cap"] = 0
   860	        else:
   861	            notes.extend(apply_aimd(account_state, counters, knobs, live[name], now,
   862	                                    floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling))
   863	            account_state["cap"] = clamp(account_state["cap"], floor, ceiling)
   864	        update_measurement(account_state, counters, live[name], now,
   865	                           measured_hold_s=windows["measured_hold_s"])
   866	        if notes:
   867	            account_state["last_change"] = ts(now)
   868	        caps[name] = int(account_state["cap"])
   869	        measured = account_state["measured_limit"]
   870	        estimate["accounts"][name] = {
   871	            "nominal": entry["nominal_limit"], "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"],
   872	            "cap_now": caps[name], "live": live[name], "waiters": waiters,
   873	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m_by_class": counters["deaths_by_class"],
   874	            "measured_limit": measured,
   875	            "observed_refusal_floor": account_state["observed_refusal_floor"],
   876	            "external_inferred": (None if measured is None else entry["nominal_limit"]
   877	                                  - entry["external_reserved"] - int(measured)),
   878	            "health": health["state"], "updated": ts(now)}

   880	            "cap": caps[name], "live": live[name], "floor": floor, "ceiling": ceiling,
   881	            "health": health["state"], "health_was": was, "health_action": action,
   882	            "health_reason": health.get("reason") or "",
   883	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m": counters["deaths"],
   884	            "neutral_5m": counters["neutral"], "measured_limit": measured,
   885	            "enabled": bool(entry["enabled"]), "endpoint": entry["endpoint"],
   886	            "label": entry.get("label") or name, "note": entry.get("note") or "",
   887	            "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"], "notes": notes}

   890	            "disabled_by": health.get("disabled_by") or "", "since": health.get("since"),

   897	            "backoff_s": health.get("backoff_s")}
   898	        if not dry_run:
   899	            _write_json(health_path(name), health)
   900	
   901	    for stale in [name for name in state["accounts"] if name not in accounts]:
   902	        state["accounts"].pop(stale)

   905	                 accounts_source=run_mode.get("accounts_source", ""))
   906	    summary["max_codex"] = sum(caps.values())
   907	    summary["accounts_source"] = run_mode.get("accounts_source", "")

   914	        # and dispatch.sh already read.  The per-account files stay exactly as

   489	def parse_directives(text: str) -> list[dict]:
   490	    """Every ``ACCOUNTS:`` line of a comment, parsed or rejected by name.
   491	
   492	    Returns one record per directive line::
   493	
   494	        {"raw": "...", "name": "second", "fields": {"ceiling": "20"}, "error": ""}
   495	
   496	    A record with a non-empty ``error`` is reported back to the owner rather than
   497	    applied, so a typo is answered instead of ignored.  Nothing outside an
   498	    ``ACCOUNTS:`` line is looked at: the rest of the comment is prose.
   499	    """
   500	    out: list[dict] = []
   501	    for line in (text or "").splitlines():
   502	        match = DIRECTIVE_RE.match(line)
   503	        if not match:
   504	            continue
   505	        record = {"raw": sanitize(line.strip(), 200), "name": "", "fields": {},
   506	                  "error": ""}
   507	        tokens = match.group("rest").split()
   508	        name = tokens[0] if tokens else ""
   509	        if not NAME_RE.match(name or ""):
   510	            record["error"] = (f"the first word after 'ACCOUNTS:' must be an account "
   511	                               f"name matching {NAME_RE.pattern}, got {name!r}")
   512	            out.append(record)
   513	            continue
   514	        record["name"] = name
   515	        for token in tokens[1:]:
   516	            assignment = ASSIGN_RE.match(token)
   517	            if not assignment:
   518	                record["error"] = (f"{token!r} is not a 'field=value' assignment; the "
   519	                                   "form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> "
   520	                                   "[reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")
   521	                break
   522	            key = assignment.group("key").lower()
   523	            if key not in DIRECTIVE_FIELDS:
   524	                record["error"] = (f"field {key!r} may not be set from a comment; this "
   525	                                   f"channel carries {', '.join(DIRECTIVE_FIELDS)} only "
   526	                                   "(an endpoint or a codex home is a path on the host "
   527	                                   "and is set with accounts.sh)")
   528	                break
   529	            record["fields"][key] = assignment.group("value")
   530	        if not record["error"] and not record["fields"]:
   531	            record["error"] = ("no field to set; the form is 'ACCOUNTS: <name> "
   532	                               "ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>] [enabled=true|false]'")
   533	        out.append(record)
   534	    return out

   537	def apply_directives(text: str, *, root: Path | None = None, actor: str,
   538	                     origin: str = "") -> list[str]:
   539	    """Apply every directive of one comment; returns the owner-facing lines.
   540	
   541	    Each line begins with ``applied:`` or ``rejected:`` and names the account and
   542	    what changed, so the confirmation reply says exactly what took effect.  A
   543	    rejected directive never blocks the others: the owner gets one answer per
   544	    line they wrote.
   545	    """
   546	    directives = parse_directives(text)
   547	    if not directives:
   548	        return []
   549	    entries = load(root)
   550	    if entries is None:
   551	        return [f"rejected: {record['raw']} — no {accounts_path(root)} on the host yet; "
   552	                "the run brief has not been applied" for record in directives]
   553	    results: list[str] = []
   554	    dirty = False
   555	    for record in directives:
   556	        if record["error"]:
   557	            results.append(f"rejected: {record['raw']} — {record['error']}")
   558	            continue
   559	        try:
   560	            changes = apply_fields(entries, record["name"], record["fields"])
   561	        except AccountsError as exc:
   562	            results.append(f"rejected: {record['raw']} — {exc}")
   563	            continue
   564	        dirty = True
   565	        results.append(f"applied: {record['name']} " +
   566	                       ("; ".join(changes) if changes
   567	                        else "already at the requested values"))
   568	    if dirty:
   569	        save(entries, root=root, actor=actor, action="inbox",
   570	             detail=f"{origin}: " + " | ".join(results),
   571	             source=f"owner inbox comment {origin}".strip())
   572	    return results

   193	def sweep(issue: int, *, dry_run: bool = False, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
   194	          max_age_min: int = DEFAULT_MAX_AGE_MIN,
   195	          now: datetime | None = None) -> list[str]:
   196	    """Answer every unanswered, recent ``ACCOUNTS:`` comment; the report lines.
   197	
   198	    Two bounds, both necessary: `limit` caps how far back the scan goes, and
   199	    `max_age_min` caps how old a directive may be and still be acted on.  A
   200	    stale one is reported in the janitor's line and NOT replied to, so the
   201	    owner's "no reply means it was not applied" rule still holds and a repeat
   202	    comment is answered normally.
   203	    """
   204	    login, source = owner_login()
   205	    comments = gh_common.api(f"issues/{issue}/comments", paginate=True) or []
   206	    applied = set(applied_ids())
   207	    report: list[str] = []
   208	    for row in comments[-limit:]:
   209	        body = row.get("body") or ""
   210	        if MARKER in body:  # one of our own replies
   211	            continue
   212	        directives = accounts_file.parse_directives(body)
   213	        if not directives:
   214	            continue
   215	        comment_id = int(row.get("id") or 0)
   216	        if not comment_id or already_answered(comments, comment_id):
   217	            continue
   218	        if comment_id in applied:
   219	            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} was already "
   220	                          "applied but its reply did not post; not applying it again")
   221	            continue
   222	        age = comment_age_min(row, now)
   223	        if max_age_min > 0 and age is not None and age > max_age_min:
   224	            report.append(
   225	                f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} is {age:.0f} min old "
   226	                f"(bound {max_age_min} min); NOT applied and not answered — capacity "
   227	                "advice this old is worse than none. Repeat it to apply it.")
   228	            continue
   229	        author = str((row.get("user") or {}).get("login") or "")
   230	        if author != login:
   231	            # Reported, never replied to.  A public reply echoing a stranger's
   232	            # text back let anyone with comment access make the bot comment once
   233	            # per comment they wrote.  The author check is the load-bearing part
   234	            # and is unchanged; the attempt is still visible, in the janitor's
   235	            # own report, where the owner reads it.
   236	            report += [
   237	                f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} by "
   238	                f"@{sanitize(author, 40) or 'an unknown account'}: ignored — this "
   239	                f"channel applies only the repository owner's comments ({login}, "
   240	                f"from {source}); {record['raw']}"
   241	                for record in directives]
   242	            continue
   243	        if dry_run:
   244	            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: comment {comment_id} by @{author}: "
   245	                          f"{len(directives)} directive(s) would be applied (dry run)")
   246	            continue
   247	        record_applied(comment_id)
   248	        results = accounts_file.apply_directives(
   249	            body, actor=f"github:{author}", origin=f"#{issue} comment {comment_id}")
   250	        gh_common.ensure_pr_comment(issue, reply_marker(comment_id),
   251	                                    render_reply(comment_id, author, results))
   252	        for line in results:
   253	            report.append(f"accounts-inbox: #{issue} comment {comment_id} "
   254	                          f"by @{author}: {line}")
   255	    if not report:
   256	        report.append("accounts-inbox: no new ACCOUNTS: directive")
   257	    return report

   560	    """Classify a captured session ending.
   561	
   562	    Returns ``{failure_class, failure_detail, failure_endpoint, retries_seen}``.
   563	
   564	    ``unknown`` is the safe default and the capacity controller must treat it as
   565	    **neutral** — neither an increase nor a decrease — so that a provider
   566	    wording change degrades to today's static behaviour rather than collapsing
   567	    the cap.  Classes:
   568	
   569	    ``concurrency_limit``  the account is at its real limit (retryable)
   570	    ``endpoint_5xx``       the endpoint is down (retryable, trips health)
   571	    ``retries_exhausted``  the client gave up reconnecting (retryable)
   572	    ``timeout``            our own session guard fired (NOT retryable)
   573	    ``task_failure``       a clean nonzero exit with model output (NOT retryable)
   574	    ``none``               exit 0
   575	    ``unknown``            anything else — neutral
   576	    """

   582	    retry_total = 0
   583	    for match in RETRY_RE.finditer(text):
   584	        seen, total = int(match.group(1)), int(match.group(2))
   585	        retries_seen = max(retries_seen, seen)
   586	        retry_total = max(retry_total, total)
   587	
   588	    matched_class = ""
   589	    matched_pattern = ""
   590	    for name in FAILURE_CLASS_ORDER:
   591	        for pattern in table.get(name) or ():
   592	            if pattern.lower() in lowered:
   593	                matched_class, matched_pattern = name, pattern
   594	                break
   595	        if matched_class:
   596	            break

   598	    if not matched_class and retry_total and retries_seen >= retry_total:
   599	        matched_class, matched_pattern = "retries_exhausted", f"{retries_seen}/{retry_total}"

   601	    endpoint = None
   602	    host = URL_HOST_RE.search(text)
   603	    if host:
   604	        candidate = host.group(1).lower().strip(".")
   605	        if LABEL_RE.match(candidate):

   607	
   608	    if matched_class:

   611	        failure_class, detail = "timeout", f"killed by the session guard (exit {exit_code})"

   616	    else:
   617	        failure_class, detail = "unknown", ""

   621	        "failure_detail": sanitize_text(detail, limit=200) or None,
   622	        "failure_endpoint": endpoint,
   623	        "retries_seen": retries_seen,
