   536	    """Write one cap file, refusing anything that is not a nonneg integer.
   537	
   538	    The guard is the point: an empty or non-numeric cap file makes every dispatch
   539	    exit 4 with ``invalid literal for int()``, silently stopping all work.
   540	    """
   541	    text = f"{int(value)}\n"
   542	    _require(int(value) >= 0 and text.strip().isdecimal(),
   543	             f"{path}: refusing to write a cap that is not a nonnegative integer ({value!r})")
   544	    atomic_write(path, text)

   547	def write_cap_files(caps: dict[str, int]) -> int:
   548	    """Write the legacy derived outputs; ``max-codex`` is mechanically the sum.
   549	
   550	    It therefore cannot disagree with the per-account files.  It is a display and
   551	    lane-parallelism value only: admission reads the per-account files
   552	    (``local/protocols/capacity.md`` §4).
   553	    """
   554	    effective = {name: int(value) for name, value in caps.items()}
   555	    directory = watchdog_dir()
   556	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   557	    # A cap file for an account that has dropped out of the configured set is
   558	    # ZEROED, not deleted.  Deleting it would break the "never an empty read"
   559	    # property; leaving its old number is worse still, because that stale file is
   560	    # exactly what `account_router.account_names()` picks up from its
   561	    # ``max-codex-*`` glob when accounts.json is unreadable — a key the owner
   562	    # removed would go on being admitted at the ceiling it had when they removed
   563	    # it.  The two historical names keep a file unconditionally, so a reader that
   564	    # predates this layer still finds a number.
   565	    stale = sorted(path.name[len("max-codex-"):] for path in
   566	                   directory.glob("max-codex-*")
   567	                   if path.is_file() and path.name != "max-codex"
   568	                   and path.name[len("max-codex-"):] not in effective)
   569	    for name in (*DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS, *stale,
   570	                 *(name for name in effective if name not in DEFAULT_ACCOUNTS)):
   571	        _write_cap_file(directory / f"max-codex-{name}", effective.get(name, 0))
   572	    _write_cap_file(directory / "max-codex", sum(effective.values()))
   573	    return sum(effective.values())

   579	def probe_account(account: str, codex_home: str, timeout_s: int) -> bool:
   580	    """One bounded, read-only probe of *account*'s endpoint.
   581	
   582	    A health check, not a work session: read-only sandbox, no persona, no task,
   583	    no worktree write, nothing appended to ``sessions.jsonl``.  Its record is the
   584	    health file and the ``capacity`` row in ``stages.jsonl``.
   585	    ``MIPSTARRE_CAPACITY_PROBE_CMD`` replaces the command for the health tests
   586	    and for a dry run on a host without ``codex``.
   587	    """
   588	    override = os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_CAPACITY_PROBE_CMD")
   589	    command = shlex.split(override) if override else [
   590	        os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_CODEX_BIN", "codex"), "exec", "--sandbox", "read-only",
   591	        "-C", str(repo_root()), "--", "Reply with the single word: ok"]
   592	    env = dict(os.environ, MIPSTARRE_CAPACITY_PROBE=account)
   593	    if codex_home:
   594	        env["CODEX_HOME"] = str(Path(codex_home).expanduser())
   595	    try:
   596	        return subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_s,
   597	                              env=env).returncode == 0

   602	def _try_probe(account: str, codex_home: str, timeout_s: int) -> tuple[bool, bool]:
   603	    """``(ran, succeeded)`` — single-flight, so two ticks cannot probe at once."""
   604	    capacity_dir().mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   605	    with (capacity_dir() / f"probe-{account}.lock").open("a") as lock:
   606	        try:
   607	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   608	        except OSError:
   609	            return False, False
   610	        try:
   611	            return True, probe_account(account, codex_home, timeout_s)
   612	        finally:
   613	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

   616	def update_health(account: str, health: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, now: datetime,
   617	                  *, no_probe: bool, codex_home: str, probe_timeout_s: int) -> str:
   618	    """Advance the endpoint health machine one tick; returns what it did.
   619	
   620	    Independent of AIMD in both directions: a refusal never changes health and a
   621	    5xx never runs the AIMD arithmetic.
   622	
   623	    Two kinds of trip, one machine.  ``endpoint_5xx`` says the ENDPOINT is down
   624	    and needs ``fivexx_threshold`` deaths inside ``fivexx_window_s`` — a single
   625	    502 is noise.  ``auth`` and ``insufficient_balance`` say the KEY is unusable
   626	    and trip at ``disable_threshold`` (1): a `401` is not a statistic, and
   627	    retrying an invalid key at any concurrency produces nothing but dead
   628	    sessions.  Both write the REASON into the health file, because "cap 0" with
   629	    no reason is the state the owner had to diagnose by reading captures on
   630	    2026-09-12; the way back is the same half-open probe, with the key-invalid
   631	    backoff starting longer (``disable_backoff_s``) since a key does not become
   632	    valid again in thirty seconds.
   633	    """
   634	    fivexx = len(counters["fivexx_times"])
   635	    disabling = len(counters.get("disable_times") or ())
   636	    base = knobs["probe_backoff_s"]
   637	    disable_base = max(base, int(knobs.get("disable_backoff_s",
   638	                                           _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_backoff_s"])))
   639	    health.update(consecutive_5xx=fivexx, key_failures=disabling, updated=ts(now))
   640	    if health["state"] != "down":
   641	        if disabling >= int(knobs.get("disable_threshold",
   642	                                      _DISABLE_DEFAULTS["disable_threshold"])):
   643	            detail = counters.get("disable_detail") or ""
   644	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0,
   645	                          backoff_s=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]),
   646	                          reason=f"{counters.get('disable_class') or 'key'}: "
   647	                                 f"{detail or 'the key was refused'}",
   648	                          disabled_by=counters.get("disable_class") or "key",
   649	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(
   650	                              seconds=min(disable_base, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"]))))
   651	            return "trip"
   652	        if fivexx >= knobs["fivexx_threshold"]:
   653	            health.update(state="down", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0, backoff_s=base,
   654	                          reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} deaths in "
   655	                                 f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s",
   656	                          disabled_by="endpoint_5xx",
   657	                          next_probe_at=ts(now + timedelta(seconds=base)))
   658	            return "trip"
   659	        if fivexx:
   660	            if health["state"] != "degraded":
   661	                health.update(state="degraded", since=ts(now),
   662	                              reason=f"endpoint_5xx: {fivexx} death(s) in "
   663	                                     f"{knobs['fivexx_window_s']}s, below the "
   664	                                     f"threshold of {knobs['fivexx_threshold']}")
   665	            return "degraded"
   666	        if health["state"] != "up":
   667	            health.update(state="up", since=ts(now), reason="")
   668	            return "clear"
   669	        return "none"
   670	    if no_probe:  # an operator hold, or a key the brief disabled
   671	        return "probe-held"
   672	    due = parse_ts(health.get("next_probe_at"))
   673	    if due is not None and now < due:
   674	        return "probe-waiting"
   675	    ran, ok = _try_probe(account, codex_home, probe_timeout_s)
   676	    if not ran:
   677	        return "probe-inflight"
   678	    if not ok:
   679	        health["probes_ok"] = 0
   680	        health["backoff_s"] = min(int(health["backoff_s"]) * 2, knobs["probe_backoff_max_s"])
   681	        health["next_probe_at"] = ts(now + timedelta(seconds=health["backoff_s"]))
   682	        return "probe-failed"
   683	    health["probes_ok"] = int(health["probes_ok"]) + 1
   684	    if health["probes_ok"] < knobs["probes_to_recover"]:
   685	        health["next_probe_at"] = ts(now + timedelta(seconds=base))
   686	        return "probe-ok"
   687	    health.update(state="up", since=ts(now), probes_ok=0, consecutive_5xx=0,
   688	                  key_failures=0, reason="", disabled_by="",
   689	                  backoff_s=base, next_probe_at=None)
   690	    return "recovered"

   695	
   696	def clamp(value: int, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> int:
   697	    """Into ``[floor, ceiling]``; the ceiling wins when the two cross."""
   698	    return max(min(floor, ceiling), min(ceiling, int(value)))

   700	
   701	def apply_aimd(account_state: dict, counters: dict, knobs: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   702	               *, floor: int, ceiling: int) -> list[str]:
   703	    """Decrease first, so a refusal cannot be overtaken by an increase."""
   704	    notes: list[str] = []
   705	    aimd = knobs["aimd"]
   706	    window = timedelta(seconds=aimd["quiet_window_s"])
   707	    cap = int(account_state["cap"])
   708	    cursor = parse_ts(account_state.get("refusal_cursor"))
   709	    fresh = [moment for moment in counters["refusal_times"] if cursor is None or moment > cursor]
   710	    if fresh:
   711	        until = parse_ts(account_state.get("decrease_window_until"))
   712	        if until is None or now > until:
   713	            # The FIRST refusal of a window: step just under the concurrency that
   714	            # was refused.  ``live`` is sampled at the tick that observes it,
   715	            # which is the closest the controller gets to the moment of refusal —
   716	            # but when the refused sessions have already died it is 0 or 1, and a
   717	            # raw ``live - 1`` would collapse the cap to the floor and then climb
   718	            # back one slot per quiet window (an hour from 1 to 30 with the
   719	            # shipped defaults).  Fall back to what the account is KNOWN to have
   720	            # sustained before believing an instantaneous zero.
   721	            evidence = [value for value in
   722	                        (account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor"),
   723	                         account_state.get("measured_limit"))
   724	                        if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)]
   725	            basis = live if live > 1 else max([live] + evidence)
   726	            cap = max(floor, min(cap, basis - 1))
   727	            account_state["decrease_window_until"] = ts(now + window)
   728	            notes.append(f"decrease(first) live={live} basis={basis} -> {cap}")
   729	            observed = basis
   730	        else:
   731	            cap = max(floor, math.ceil(cap * float(aimd["decrease"])))
   732	            notes.append(f"decrease(x{aimd['decrease']}) -> {cap}")
   733	            observed = live
   734	        account_state.update(refusal_cursor=ts(max(fresh)), quiet_since=None)
   735	        if observed >= 1:  # a zero census is not evidence that one slot refused
   736	            seen = account_state.get("observed_refusal_floor")
   737	            account_state["observed_refusal_floor"] = (
   738	                observed if seen is None else min(int(seen), observed))
   739	    # ``live >= cap - 1`` keeps the cap honest: a cap nobody uses is not evidence
   740	    # of headroom.
   741	    if (not counters["refusals"] and not counters["deaths"]
   742	            and account_state["health"] == "up" and live >= cap - 1):
   743	        started = parse_ts(account_state.get("quiet_since"))
   744	        if started is None:
   745	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   746	        elif now - started >= window:
   747	            if cap < ceiling:
   748	                cap = min(ceiling, cap + int(aimd["increase"]))
   749	                notes.append(f"increase -> {cap}")
   750	            account_state["quiet_since"] = ts(now)
   751	    else:
   752	        account_state["quiet_since"] = None
   753	    account_state["cap"] = clamp(cap, floor, ceiling)
   754	    return notes

   757	def update_measurement(account_state: dict, counters: dict, live: int, now: datetime,
   758	                       *, measured_hold_s: int) -> None:
   759	    """The highest concurrency sustained *measured_hold_s* with no refusal or death."""
   760	    if counters["refusals"] or counters["deaths"]:
   761	        account_state.update(measured_since=None, measured_level=None)
   762	        return
   763	    started = parse_ts(account_state.get("measured_since"))
   764	    level = account_state.get("measured_level")
   765	    if started is None or not isinstance(level, int):
   766	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)
   767	        return
   768	    account_state["measured_level"] = min(int(level), live)
   769	    if now - started >= timedelta(seconds=measured_hold_s):
   770	        sustained, current = int(account_state["measured_level"]), account_state["measured_limit"]
   771	        if current is None or sustained > int(current):
   772	            account_state["measured_limit"] = sustained
   773	        account_state.update(measured_since=ts(now), measured_level=live)

   776	def refresh(account_state: dict, entry: dict, knobs: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:
   777	    """Ceiling and floor from the brief and the policy; returns ``(floor, ceiling)``."""
   778	    ceiling = max(0, entry["nominal_limit"] - entry["external_reserved"])
   779	    floor = min(int(knobs["floor"]), ceiling)
   780	    account_state.update(nominal_limit=entry["nominal_limit"], floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling,
   780	    account_state.update(nominal_limit=entry["nominal_limit"], floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling,
   781	                         external_reserved=entry["external_reserved"],
   782	                         enabled=entry["enabled"], endpoint=entry["endpoint"])
   783	    return floor, ceiling

   786	def seed_cap(account_state: dict, floor: int, ceiling: int, entry: dict) -> int:
   787	    """Starting cap for a run: ``min(brief ceiling, last measured limit)``."""
   788	    if not entry["enabled"]:
   789	        return 0
   790	    measured = account_state.get("measured_limit")
   791	    return clamp(max(ceiling if measured is None else min(ceiling, int(measured)), 1),
   792	                 floor, ceiling)

   795	def tick(now: datetime, *, policy: dict, run_mode: dict, state: dict,
   796	         dry_run: bool = False) -> dict:
   797	    """One control step: health, then decrease, then increase, then the clamp."""
   798	    windows, roles = policy["windows"], class_roles(policy)
   799	    disabling = disabling_classes(policy)
   800	    hold = (capacity_dir() / "hold").exists()
   801	    paused = state.get("paused_at") is not None
   802	    accounts = run_mode["accounts"]
   803	    endpoints, ambiguous = attribution_map(accounts)
   804	    lookback = max([windows["counter_window_s"]]
   805	                   + [health_knobs(policy, name)["fivexx_window_s"] for name in accounts])
   806	    rows = read_session_rows(telemetry_dir() / "sessions.jsonl",
   807	                             now - timedelta(seconds=lookback))
   808	    live, waiters = count_live(accounts), count_waiters()
   809	    summary: dict[str, Any] = {"ts": ts(now), "hold": hold, "paused": paused,
   810	                               "waiters": waiters, "accounts": {}}
   811	    if ambiguous:
   812	        # Legal (two keys on one endpoint) but worth saying once a tick: rows
   813	        # that carry only that token are attributed to neither key.
   814	        summary["ambiguous_endpoints"] = ambiguous
   815	    caps: dict[str, int] = {}
   816	    health_rows: dict[str, dict] = {}
   817	    estimate = {"schema": "mipstarre-capacity-estimate/1", "updated": ts(now), "accounts": {}}
   818	
   819	    for name, entry in accounts.items():
   820	        knobs = knobs_for(policy, name)
   821	        hknobs = health_knobs(policy, name)
   822	        counters = observe(rows, name, endpoints, roles, now,
   823	                           counter_window_s=windows["counter_window_s"],
   824	                           fivexx_window_s=hknobs["fivexx_window_s"],
   825	                           disabling=disabling)
   826	        account_state = state["accounts"].setdefault(name, new_account_state(name))
   827	        floor, ceiling = refresh(account_state, entry, knobs)
   828	        health = load_health(name, entry["endpoint"], now, hknobs["probe_backoff_s"])
   829	        was = health["state"]
   830	        # A paused run has no daemons and spends no key: `paused` joins the hold
   831	        # and the disabled account in suppressing the probe, so a pause can never
   832	        # fire `codex exec` on the owner's keys after the deadline.
   833	        action = update_health(name, health, counters, hknobs, now,
   834	                               no_probe=hold or paused or not entry["enabled"],
   835	                               codex_home=entry["codex_home"],
   836	                               probe_timeout_s=windows["probe_timeout_s"])
   837	        account_state["health"] = health["state"]
   838	        notes: list[str] = []
   839	        if hold:
   840	            notes.append("hold: cap frozen")
   841	        elif paused or not entry["enabled"]:
   842	            # BEFORE the recovery branch: a recovering endpoint must not raise
   843	            # the cap to 1 while state.json says paused (or while the brief says
   844	            # this key is off).  Pause outranks health in both directions.
   845	            if int(account_state["cap"]) != 0:  # a note per tick would be noise
   846	                notes.append("paused: cap 0" if paused
   847	                             else "disabled in the accounts file: cap 0, no probe")
   848	            account_state.update(cap=0, quiet_since=None, decrease_window_until=None)
   849	        elif action == "trip":
   850	            account_state.update(cap=0, quiet_since=None, decrease_window_until=None)
   851	            notes.append("endpoint down: cap 0")
   852	        elif action == "recovered":
   853	            # Never back to the pre-outage cap: the endpoint that just came back
   854	            # is the last thing to hand twenty sessions.
   855	            account_state.update(cap=clamp(1, floor, ceiling), quiet_since=None,
   856	                                 decrease_window_until=None, refusal_cursor=None)
   857	            notes.append(f"endpoint recovered: cap {account_state['cap']}, AIMD climbs")
   858	        elif health["state"] == "down":
   859	            account_state["cap"] = 0
   860	        else:
   861	            notes.extend(apply_aimd(account_state, counters, knobs, live[name], now,
   862	                                    floor=floor, ceiling=ceiling))
   863	            account_state["cap"] = clamp(account_state["cap"], floor, ceiling)
   864	        update_measurement(account_state, counters, live[name], now,
   865	                           measured_hold_s=windows["measured_hold_s"])
   866	        if notes:
   867	            account_state["last_change"] = ts(now)
   868	        caps[name] = int(account_state["cap"])
   869	        measured = account_state["measured_limit"]
   870	        estimate["accounts"][name] = {
   871	            "nominal": entry["nominal_limit"], "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"],
   872	            "cap_now": caps[name], "live": live[name], "waiters": waiters,
   873	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m_by_class": counters["deaths_by_class"],
   874	            "measured_limit": measured,
   875	            "observed_refusal_floor": account_state["observed_refusal_floor"],
   876	            "external_inferred": (None if measured is None else entry["nominal_limit"]
   877	                                  - entry["external_reserved"] - int(measured)),
   878	            "health": health["state"], "updated": ts(now)}
   879	        summary["accounts"][name] = {
   880	            "cap": caps[name], "live": live[name], "floor": floor, "ceiling": ceiling,
   881	            "health": health["state"], "health_was": was, "health_action": action,
   882	            "health_reason": health.get("reason") or "",
   883	            "refusals_5m": counters["refusals"], "deaths_5m": counters["deaths"],
   884	            "neutral_5m": counters["neutral"], "measured_limit": measured,
   885	            "enabled": bool(entry["enabled"]), "endpoint": entry["endpoint"],
   886	            "label": entry.get("label") or name, "note": entry.get("note") or "",
   887	            "external_reserved": entry["external_reserved"], "notes": notes}
   888	        health_rows[name] = {
   889	            "state": health["state"], "reason": health.get("reason") or "",
   890	            "disabled_by": health.get("disabled_by") or "", "since": health.get("since"),
   891	            "endpoint": entry["endpoint"], "enabled": bool(entry["enabled"]),
   892	            "cap": caps[name], "ceiling": ceiling,
   893	            "consecutive_5xx": health.get("consecutive_5xx", 0),
   894	            "key_failures": health.get("key_failures", 0),
   895	            "probes_ok": health.get("probes_ok", 0),
   896	            "next_probe_at": health.get("next_probe_at"),
   897	            "backoff_s": health.get("backoff_s")}
   898	        if not dry_run:
   899	            _write_json(health_path(name), health)
   900	
   901	    for stale in [name for name in state["accounts"] if name not in accounts]:
   902	        state["accounts"].pop(stale)
   903	        summary.setdefault("dropped", []).append(stale)
   904	    state.update(updated=ts(now), brief_ref=run_mode["brief_ref"],
   905	                 accounts_source=run_mode.get("accounts_source", ""))
   906	    summary["max_codex"] = sum(caps.values())
   907	    summary["accounts_source"] = run_mode.get("accounts_source", "")
   908	    if not dry_run:
   909	        if not hold:
   910	            summary["max_codex"] = write_cap_files(caps)
   911	        _write_json(state_path(), state)
   912	        _write_json(capacity_dir() / "limit-estimate.json", estimate)
   913	        # ONE document for every key, next to the per-account files the router
   914	        # and dispatch.sh already read.  The per-account files stay exactly as
   915	        # they are (they are the admission input); this is the owner's picture —
   916	        # which key is disabled, and the REASON, which is what the hourly per-key
   917	        # line and `accounts.sh list` quote instead of "cap 0, nobody knows why".
   918	        _write_json(capacity_dir() / "health.json",
   919	                    {"schema": HEALTH_SCHEMA, "updated": ts(now),
   920	                     "source": run_mode.get("accounts_source", ""),
   921	                     "accounts": health_rows})
   922	        summary["account_mode"] = write_account_mode(accounts)
   923	    return summary

   984	def append_stage(event: str, summary: dict, note: str) -> None:

  1004	def append_tick(summary: dict, note: str) -> Path:
  1005	    """The per-tick record: runtime state under the cache root, never committed.
  1006	
  1007	    Trimmed to the last ``TICKS_KEEP`` rows by this writer, so nobody has to
  1008	    prune it by hand and it cannot grow without bound on a long run.

  1010	    path = capacity_dir() / "ticks.jsonl"
  1011	    _append_jsonl(path, {"ts": summary.get("ts") or ts(utcnow()), "event": "tick",
  1012	                         "note": note, "capacity": summary})
  1013	    try:
  1014	        lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
  1015	        if len(lines) > TICKS_KEEP:
  1016	            tmp = path.with_suffix(".jsonl.tmp")
  1017	            tmp.write_text("\n".join(lines[-TICKS_KEEP:]) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
  1018	            os.replace(tmp, path)
  1019	    except OSError:
  1020	        pass  # a trim failure must never fail a control step
  1021	    return path

  1048	    """``_lock`` or a named failure — never ``None`` reaching a ``.close()``.
  1049	
  1050	    ``flock`` can fail on a blocking wait too (EINTR is reachable), and an
  1051	    unguarded ``lock.close()`` in a ``finally`` turns that into an
  1052	    ``AttributeError`` traceback that ``main``'s handler does not catch.

  1054	    handle = _lock(blocking)
  1055	    if handle is None:
  1056	        raise ControllerError(

  1058	            "controller holds it or the lock could not be acquired. Nothing was "
  1059	            "written: the cap files are exactly as they were.")

  1387	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
  1388	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
  1389	                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
  1390	    parser.add_argument("--policy", type=Path, help="capacity policy (default: the checkout's)")

  1392	    parser.add_argument("--now", type=_moment, help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
  1393	    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
  1394	    for name, handler, help_text in (
  1395	            ("init", cmd_init, "validate the brief and seed the starting caps"),
  1396	            ("tick", cmd_tick, "one control step (the 60 s loop)"),
  1397	            ("set", cmd_set, "operator override of one account's cap"),
  1398	            ("pause", cmd_pause, "caps to 0, saving them inside state.json"),
  1399	            ("resume", cmd_resume, "restore the saved caps and re-enter AIMD"),
  1400	            ("probe", cmd_probe, "run the health probe now (owner-tools/accounts.sh probe)")):
  1401	        sub = subparsers.add_parser(name, help=help_text)
  1402	        sub.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
  1403	        if name == "probe":
  1404	            sub.add_argument("account", nargs="?", default="",
  1405	                             help="default: every configured account")
  1406	            sub.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
  1407	                             help="probe even while the run is paused or the caps "

  1409	        if name == "init":

  1411	                             help="discard the carried measurement as well as the run state")

  1414	            sub.add_argument("cap", type=int)
  1415	        if name == "pause":
  1416	            sub.add_argument("--reason")
  1417	        sub.set_defaults(handler=handler)

  1419	    group = status.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
  1420	    group.add_argument("--json", action="store_true")

    54	    def comment(self, body: str, login: str) -> int:

    61	            mutation=False, idempotent=False, absolute=False):
    62	        if path.startswith(f"issues/{ISSUE}/comments") and method is None:

   455	def _policy_pattern_table(table) -> dict[str, list] | None:
   456	    """The policy's failure wordings as ``class -> patterns``, or ``None``.
   457	
   458	    ``local/capacity-policy.json`` writes the LIST form the capacity controller
   459	    validates — one object per class carrying ``failure_class``, ``counts_as``
   460	    and ``patterns`` — while older knobs wrote a plain object.  Reading only the
   461	    object form is how the policy's ``auth`` and ``insufficient_balance``
   462	    wordings never reached the classifier: the whole table was discarded without
   463	    a word, every quota refusal classified ``unknown``, and ``unknown`` is
   464	    neutral, so a dead key kept its cap.  Both shapes are read here so the file
   465	    the controller validates and the table the classifier uses cannot disagree.
   466	    """
   467	    if isinstance(table, dict):
   468	        return table
   469	    if not isinstance(table, list):
   470	        return None
   471	    out: dict[str, list] = {}
   472	    for row in table:
   473	        if not isinstance(row, dict):
   474	            continue
   475	        name = row.get("failure_class")
   476	        if isinstance(name, str) and name:
   477	            out[name] = row.get("patterns")
   478	    return out or None

     3	#
     4	# Usage:
     5	#   accounts.sh list [--json]

    20	# What it edits: ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json, the live source of
    21	# truth for which keys exist, what their CEILINGS are, and whether the pipeline may

    23	# tick and every reservation, so a change here reaches admission within 60 seconds
    24	# with no session prompted, no brief re-applied and nothing restarted.
    25	#
    26	# `ceiling` is a ceiling and never a target: the controller's AIMD discovery runs
    27	# below it and may never exceed `ceiling - external_reserved`.  Lowering it takes
    28	# effect at the next tick; raising it lets the additive creep continue.
    29	# `enabled false` is cap 0 immediately and no probes, and so is `remove`.
    30	#
    31	# Raising a ceiling is a PERMISSION, not a jump: AIMD then creeps +1 per quiet
    32	# window (120 s by default) and only while the key is saturated, so ten recovered
    33	# slots take twenty minutes of real demand.  `accounts.sh cap <name> <n>` is the
    34	# one immediate lever — it sets the effective cap now, clamped to the ceiling and
    35	# recorded by the controller.  Set the ceiling first; the cap cannot exceed it.
    36	#
    37	# Every write is atomic (temp file + rename) and appends one line to

     3	
     4	Historically this file held only the candidate scan.  It now also owns every
     5	*record format* the daemon reads and writes, so that the formats have one
     6	writer, one reader and a unit test instead of being re-derived by `grep` in
     7	bash (full-speed-mode v2 design §3.2-§3.5, work item W5).

    12	                   clean | adj | retire | offconv | skip.  Without ``--all``
    13	                   only clean/adj/retire lines are printed, which is the
    14	                   historical output plus the retirement pass.
    15	    classify       classify a lane / merge log into one of the six failure
    16	                   classes, printing ``CLASS<TAB>REASON``.
    17	    marker-write   write (or refresh) a classed failure marker, the JSON
    18	                   record that replaced ``touch pr<N>.failed``.
    19	    marker-check   decide whether a marker still blocks its PR.  Exit 0 =
    20	                   blocked, 10 = clear, 2 = usage.

    22	                   ``--json-out`` also the machine-readable snapshot that

    24	    latency        append one ``merge-latency`` row.

    26	    slots          free worker slots, read through local/bin/account_router.py.

     2	# install.sh — the ONE deployment path for the operator tools (design full-speed-v2 §7).
     3	#
     4	# Operator scripts drive tmux, the crontab and the host process table, so they cannot be
     5	# run from the checkout (which is mid-merge for minutes at a time).  They are therefore
     6	# COPIED to ~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/owner-bin/ by this installer and never edited on the
     7	# host: on 2026-09-12 three versions of the lane runner ran at once, `merge-daemon-v9h.sh`
     8	# called a `/tmp/merge-v2.sh` that does not exist, and the shim was patched by an
     9	# `assert old in s` here-doc against a 90-character substring.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   install.sh [--force] [--compat-tmp] [--crons] [--start-loops] [--dry-run]
    13	#   install.sh --verify                 # dependency/hash check (the merge daemon's gate)
    14	#   install.sh --record <name>          # re-record a regenerated file (run_mode.py set speed)
    15	#
    16	# Options:
    17	#   --force        overwrite a deployed copy whose hash matches no released version.
    18	#                  The previous copy is MOVED to owner-bin/attic/<ts>/, never deleted.
    19	#   --start-loops  start capacityd.sh (the 60 s capacity controller loop) if it is not
    20	#                  already running and no stop file holds it.  Without a running
    21	#                  controller nothing writes watchdog/max-codex-*, the caps stay frozen
    22	#                  at whatever seeded them, there is no AIMD, no 5xx trip and no
    23	#                  half-open probe — the 2026-09-12 situation, recovered by hand — and on
    24	#                  a fresh host lane.sh:wait_for_slot fails closed with
    25	#                  `no-capacity-record`.  The merge daemon and the goal keeper are NOT
    26	#                  started here: owner-resume.sh owns those (design §5).
    27	#   --compat-tmp   create /tmp/<name> SYMLINKS into owner-bin/ so anything still invoking
    28	#                  a historical /tmp path runs versioned code.  Nothing is ever written or
    29	#                  edited in /tmp; an existing regular file there is refused, not clobbered.
    30	#   --crons        run install-crons.sh afterwards (crontab regenerated from run-mode).
    31	#   --dry-run      print the plan and touch nothing (implies --dry-run for --crons too).
    32	#   --dest DIR     install into DIR instead of $MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT/owner-bin (tests).
    33	#   --compat-dir D create the compat symlinks in D instead of /tmp (tests).
    34	#   --speed S      render the PATH shim for speed S instead of asking run_mode.py (tests).
    35	#
    36	# What is written under owner-bin/:
    37	#   <tool>              the deployed copy, mode from the table below

    40	#   manifest.accepted   every hash this release accepts for a name; the PATH shim has two
    41	#                       (the fast and the default rendering), because run_mode.py set speed
    42	#                       regenerates it in place
    43	#   repo-root           the checkout this release was installed from

  1550	was impossible, and every such change had to be typed to a session that had to be
  1551	idle to receive it.

   121	    """The account with the most headroom, as a fraction of its own cap.
   122	
   123	    The rule is unchanged for two accounts — ``live[0]*caps[1] <= live[1]*caps[0]``
   124	    is exactly "the first account's occupancy is no higher" — and generalizes to

   126	    entry so a two-account file keeps preferring ``primary``.  A zero cap is
   127	    never chosen: `reserve` has already filtered it out, and treating it as
   128	    infinitely free is how a dead endpoint attracted every dispatch.

   130	    best, best_key = names[0], None
   131	    for index, name in enumerate(names):
   132	        cap = caps[index]
   133	        if cap <= 0:
   134	            continue
   135	        key = (live[index] * 1.0 / cap, index)

   302	def resume_model(thread: str, registry: Path, homes: dict[str, Path]) -> str:
   303	    """Require observed model affinity; a new default cannot relabel an old thread."""
   304	    observed = [row.get('effective_model') for row in session_rows(registry)
   305	                if row.get('thread_id') == thread and row.get('effective_model')]
   306	    for home in homes.values():
   307	        for area in ('sessions', 'archived_sessions'):
   308	            for rollout in (home / area).rglob(f'rollout-*{thread}.jsonl'):
   309	                for row in session_rows(rollout):
   310	                    if row.get('type') == 'turn_context' and row.get('payload', {}).get('model'):
   311	                        observed.append(row['payload']['model'])
   312	    if not observed or len(set(observed)) != 1:
   313	        raise ValueError('resume model is unknown or mixed; use a fresh linked assignment')

   317	def continuation(path: Path, registry: Path, worktree: Path, issue: str) -> dict:
   318	    """Validate an operator checkpoint handoff without changing the old thread or budget."""
   319	    request = json.loads(path.read_text())
   320	    rows = session_rows(registry)
   321	    previous = next(row for row in reversed(rows) if row.get('name') == request['previous_session'])
   322	    if (previous.get('status') not in ('done', 'failed', 'archived') or
   323	            not is_account_name(previous.get('account')) or not previous.get('thread_id') or
   324	            str(previous.get('issue')) != issue):
   325	        raise ValueError('continuation requires a terminal, same-issue predecessor with affinity')
   326	    checkpoint = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(worktree), 'rev-parse', '--verify',

   328	    subprocess.run(['git', '-C', str(worktree), 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor',
   329	                    checkpoint, 'HEAD'], check=True, capture_output=True)
   330	    budget_path = Path(request['budget_file']).resolve(strict=True)
   331	    budget = json.loads(budget_path.read_text())
   332	    if (not budget['anchor'] or previous['name'] not in budget['sessions'] or
   333	            not 0 < budget['attempts'] < budget['attempt_limit'] or
   334	            budget['working_seconds'] < previous.get('wall_s', 0)):
   335	        raise ValueError('continuation requires the shared, charged, unexhausted budget')
   336	    prior = resume_continuation(registry, previous['thread_id'])

   349	def reserve(root: Path, requested: str, pid: int, wait: int, dry_run: bool = False) -> str:
   350	    """Reserve one worker slot under the lock shared by all dispatchers.
   351	
   352	    ``watchdog/drain`` is checked on every poll iteration, before the lock, and
   353	    raises `DrainRequested` so a queued dispatch releases itself during a pause
   354	    instead of being killed.  Absent file, absent health file: unchanged
   355	    behaviour in every respect.
   356	    """
   357	    if (requested != 'auto' and not is_account_name(requested)) or pid <= 0 or wait < 0:
   358	        raise ValueError('expected a valid account, positive pid and nonnegative wait')
   359	    accounts = root / "accounts"
   360	    accounts.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   361	    deadline = time.monotonic() + wait
   362	    while True:
   363	        if (root / "watchdog" / "drain").exists():
   364	            raise DrainRequested('drain in progress; no reservation made')
   365	        with (accounts / "router.lock").open("a") as lock:
   366	            fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   367	            # Re-read per iteration, inside the lock: a waiter queued for half an
   368	            # hour must see the key the owner added, the ceiling they raised and
   369	            # the account they disabled, without being restarted.
   370	            names = account_names(root)
   371	            if requested != 'auto' and requested not in names:
   372	                raise ValueError(
   373	                    f'{requested!r} is not one of the configured accounts '
   374	                    f'({", ".join(names)}); add it with owner-tools/accounts.sh add')
   375	            caps = effective_caps(root, names)
   376	            live = [len(live_pids(accounts / account)) for account in names]
   377	            free = [index for index, account in enumerate(names)
   378	                    if live[index] < caps[index] and requested in ('auto', account)]
   379	            if free:
   380	                # Only the accounts with a free slot compete, exactly as the
   381	                # two-account form did: a full account is not a candidate.
   382	                selected = (names[free[0]] if len(free) == 1 else choose_account(
   383	                    [live[index] for index in free], [caps[index] for index in free],
   384	                    tuple(names[index] for index in free)))
   385	                if not dry_run:
   386	                    (accounts / selected / str(pid)).touch()
   387	                return selected
   388	            remaining = deadline - time.monotonic()
   389	            if dry_run or remaining <= 0:
   390	                raise ValueError('account capacity exhausted; no reservation made')

item.text: The controller itself largely preserves the intended hot-reload and health state machine, but its surrounding contracts expose two more edge cases worth checking: manual recovery can be replayed against the same recent failure, and the live schema explicitly allows a zero pipeline share. I’m tracing those through pause/resume and the dispatcher before fixing the final findings set.
